articles.title: Antonio Brown used an offensive, derogatory slur against Caleb Williams after a locker room video with Case Keenum went viral
articles.summary: This is the second time that Antonio Brown has taken a social media dig at Caleb Williams.
articles.body: This is the second time that Antonio Brown has taken a social media dig at Caleb Williams.A viral locker room clip showed Williams standing in the background while Case Keenum gave his Chicago Bears vs. Philadelphia Eagles 27-7 winning speech. Brown took a screenshot of the clip and added a cheap caption directed at the young quarterback.The X post included an offensive, homophobic, derogatory slur. For the second time, Brown called Williams “Fa*got of the Week.” Back in 2025, Brown labeled Williams “Fa*got of the Day” after a viral tweet claimed Williams wasn't interested in girls as a kid because he was too locked into football.Antonio Brown’s comment follows a viral video of Caleb Williams in the locker room with Case KeenumCaleb Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He did not play against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3. Case Keenum served as his backup QB. Keenum led the team to a win over the Eagles, throwing for 247 yards and 2 touchdowns and scoring a rushing touchdown.Following the victory, Keenum received the game ball in the locker room celebration. While Keenum gave his memorable speech, Williams stood behind him in a bathrobe, hands folded and a bright smile on his face. Antonio Brown took a screenshot of that unusual moment and posted it on his X.The former Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver used a homophobic, derogatory slur and labeled Williams his “Fa*got of the Week.” There is no end to the kind of weird, adulterated posts Brown showcases on his X account. But this one stood apart from the others, especially because of the offensive nature of the insult.Brown has previously used provocative and controversial labels while targeting athletes and public figures on his X account.Williams has not responded to the post. He may treat it the same way he treated his several other AI-generated posts. One that had him crying on the field after he chipped his nail polish. The other when he posed provocatively for an NFL rivalry jersey photoshoot.Just that it was Case Keenum’s big night, and it somehow looked like Caleb Williams wanted to own it. Yes, it’s his team. Yes, Keenum’s a backup. But who plays on the gridiron and wins the battles for the franchise - matters the most.Caleb Williams’ nonstop controversy overshadows Case Keenum’s victoryThe 38-year-old quarterback Case Keenum returned to the gridiron after 1,009 days. He played as he’d never played before. This was his one chance to prove his worth. He helped beat the Jalen Hurts-led Philadelphia Eagles by a tormenting 27-7 score.When it was his time to share his joy with the team that helped him win, an injured [almost] franchise quarterback snatched his spotlight.When Caleb Williams could have easily stood in front of Keenum, listening to his victory speech like the rest of the team, he chose to stand right behind him - probably knowing for a fact that he was being recorded. And that’s how he became the hero behind the actual hero.He took the footage to the next level. As though Keenum was playing for him, not his team. Anyhow, the clip knew it would go viral. Caleb probably knew it would go viral, too.And viral-news-hungry gossipmongers like Antonio Brown also knew it would look great on their feed. And that’s what he did. He made the Williams’ story look louder and brighter than expected. Clearly surpassing Case Keenum’s victory case.Anyhow, Chicago improved its season record from 1-1 to 2-1. articles.title: Travis Kelce is most likely one season away from retirement; his real estate portfolio suggests he is already planning the next chapter
articles.summary: Travis Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Chiefs in March, and the contract is built so he can leave after this season.
articles.body: Travis Kelce signed a one-year, $12 million deal with the Chiefs in March, and the contract is built so he can leave after this season. He has not said he will. His property buying suggests he is at least preparing. Reports say Kelce closed on a $5.35 million Ohio lakefront estate about three weeks before he re-signed. Neither purchase proves anything on its own, but the timing is hard to ignore. Add the roughly $6 million Kansas mansion he already owns, and the 36-year-old looks like a player lining up where life goes after football.Is Travis Kelce one season away from retiring?Not officially. Kelce has made no announcement about 2027. The paperwork, though, leaves the door open. His 2026 deal pays $12 million and can reach $15 million. Some early reports called it a three-year, $54.7 million contract, but two of those years exist only on paper to spread out the salary cap cost. Sports Illustrated reported that the setup lets the Chiefs release him after June 1 if he retires. CBS Sports noted the contract is built for him to decide by June 2027.The football case for another year is real. Kelce led Kansas City with 76 catches and 851 yards last season and made his 11th straight Pro Bowl. Kelce turns 37 on Monday. He already holds the franchise records for catches, yards and touchdowns. But the Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, and that kind of result makes any veteran count his remaining seasons. Last November, Kelce said, "I want to give the Chiefs a good opportunity, whether I come back or not." He came back, and the same logic applies again next summer.What does Travis Kelce's real estate say about life after football?The Ohio purchase says the most. TMZ reported that Kelce bought the Bratenahl estate on March 2, months before his wedding to Taylor Swift. The Wall Street Journal said it first listed at $5.99 million. The 21,000-square-foot home, called Moyenage, was built in 1895 and sits on about 3.5 acres along Lake Erie. It is a Tudor-style mansion near Cleveland, in the state where Kelce grew up. Three weeks later, he re-signed with Kansas City.Compare that with Leawood. The Kansas mansion cost about $6 million and covers 17,000 square feet on roughly 3.5 acres, with tennis and pickleball courts and a mini-golf course. Reports link its heavy privacy to his relationship with Swift. Reports are unclear on whether he still owns his first Kansas City home, a $995,000 purchase from 2019. Leawood reads like a home built around football and fame. Bratenahl reads like one built for a slower life.One count puts the value of his three homes at $12.35 million. Together with Swift's properties, the couple's portfolio is reportedly worth about $157 million. So a career after the NFL is not a money problem. It is a question of how he spends the time. New Heights, the podcast he hosts with Jason, is an obvious answer. Jason, now retired, owns a three-unit rental house in Cleveland, so Ohio real estate is already a family habit. Kelce has not spoken publicly about why he bought the Ohio home, so the link to retirement is a reading of the timeline, not a confirmed plan.Kelce has until June 2027 to decide. articles.title: “Match made in heaven”: Patrick Mahomes’ favorite coffee company raises $18 million in total funding as Throne Sport Coffee expands to 20,000 retail locations
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes’ longtime morning coffee habit has become a multi-million-dollar business opportunity.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes’ longtime morning coffee habit has become a multi-million-dollar business opportunity. The Kansas City Chiefs QB-backed Throne Sport Coffee has now gladly reportedly secured $18 million in total funding. It has also rapidly expanded its retail footprint, with the brand targeting more than 20,000 locations across the U.S.For Mahomes, the beverage company represents a personal business investment. The three-time Super Bowl champion has openly spoken about his love for coffee. He picked up the habit during his early days with the Kansas City Chiefs. This habit eventually sparked his interest in the ready-to-drink, up-and-coming coffee market.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee inceptionThrone Sport Coffee brand launched in 2024. Patrick Mahomes became the brand’s lead investor alongside beverage industry veteran Michael Fedele. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback’s involvement goes beyond attaching his massively established name to the product.ESPN reported that Mahomes is the company’s No. 2 stakeholder. He has been involved in product development, including testing and providing feedback on the coffee. So much for a perennial coffee lover.The two-time NFL MVP’s coffee routine reportedly dates back to his rookie season in 2017. Long team meetings with the Kansas City Chiefs helped him develop a regular coffee-consuming habit. His intense interest ultimately led him to Throne Sport Coffee.“It actually started in my first year in the NFL,” Mahomes told CNBC. “I started drinking coffee a lot, just being in a lot of meetings. And I really just fell in love with it. You know, it started first as a functional thing. And then I really fell in love with just the taste and trying to make sure that what I was putting into my body was good.And so I was trying to get away from drinking all the sugary, different types of coffees that you could drink.And I was really into just black coffee, which is what I was drinking on a day-to-day basis. And so whenever Michael Fedele and Throne Sport Coffee came to me and said they had a ready-to-go, healthy cold brew coffee drink, it was like a match made in heaven.”The brand markets ready-to-drink coffee designed exclusively for customers looking for both caffeine and functional ingredients.“It was really cool to see that I got to be part of the very beginning of the tasting part of the B vitamins, the BCAAs, the electrolytes going into it and something that I could drink on a day-to-day basis. And I know that it's good stuff that's going into my body,” Mahomes added.Patrick Mahomes’ investment strategyPatrick Mahomes genuinely values his partnerships with brands including State Farm, Adidas, Doritos, T-Mobile, Subway, Coors Light, Invisalign, and Throne Sport Coffee. His relationship with Throne Sport Coffee is a little different because he’s one of the lead investors there, and he strongly believes in the product.The product is a convenient option for both athletes and everyday consumers, specifically because it is ready to drink and contains 150 milligrams of natural caffeine. The quarterback believes the product could be a good everyday coffee choice.Mahomes has had many business opportunities come his way, but he carefully chose to work with companies and products that he truly believed in. He values the people behind those businesses. He prefers partnerships that are built on long-term relationships and everlasting trust.This personalized approach extends beyond investments to his teammates, charitable work, and other areas of life. He wants to surround himself with people he believes are good and genuinely want to make a positive impact on the world.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee valuation and investor detailsAccording to Dealroom, Throne Sport Coffee has a $25 to $50 million valuation, a team of fewer than 100, and $10 to $50 million in total funding.The brand reached a massive milestone in February 2026, announcing a $10 million funding round, as per Food Business News.Throne Sport Coffee raised $10 million in a Series A round. The funds will support the brand’s next growth stage, including expanded distribution, field sales, and marketing.The company has raised a total of $18 million, according to Drew Fallon, Co-Founder and CEO of Iris Finance.The brand’s investors include professional athletes, sports executives, beverage-industry veterans, and other business founders.The brand offers several ready-to-drink varieties, including mocha java, salted caramel, mint mocha, French vanilla, and black. Its Coffee PLUS+ formula comes with caffeine, B vitamins, electrolytes, and BCAAs.Patrick Mahomes’ Throne Sport Coffee retail expansionThe brand’s fundraising helps its distribution network to grow. Food Business News reported that Throne Sport Coffee had reached roughly 7,000 retail locations by February 2026. It was nearly 5,000 in January 2025.The brand has since expanded to more than 20,000 retail locations, growing through major retailers and convenience chains such as Kroger, CVS, Whole Foods, Casey’s, QuikTrip, and Sheetz, as reported by Boardroom.That expansion comes as it debuts its new Patrick Mahomes-led “Better Fuel for Every You” campaign, part of a larger push to bring functional coffee further into the mainstream.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Travis Kelce has built an impressive fortune through his NFL career, but his spending habits reveal another side of the Kansas City Chiefs star. Some of his biggest expenses are tied to fashion, while others offer a glimpse into how the three-time Super Bowl champion enjoys life away from football. Here is a closer look at some of Travis Kelce’s most expensive possessions and purchases reported by Prestige in 2024.Travis Kelce’s luxury cars and real estateCars are among the biggest expenses in Kelce’s lifestyle. His collection was reported to be worth around USD 1.4 million, with nine vehicles ranging from classic American cars to luxury SUVs.His Rolls-Royce Ghost was listed at about USD 400,000, making it one of the standout vehicles in his garage. The vintage car gained extra attention after Kelce was seen driving Taylor Swift in it in 2023.Kelce has also invested heavily in property. One of his notable purchases was a Kansas mansion reportedly worth USD 6 million. The 17,000-square-foot home sits inside a gated community in Leawood and includes six bedrooms and six bathrooms.His property holdings also include a seven-bedroom Kansas City home purchased for about USD 995,000 in 2019, along with an Orlando condo valued at approximately USD 355,000.Travis Kelce’s expensive sneakers and fashion collectionIf there is one category that clearly reflects Kelce’s personality, it is sneakers. articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Browns' QB Situation Amid 2-1 Start
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are reportedly ready to stick by Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback after a 2-1 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are reportedly ready to stick by Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback after a 2-1 start to the 2026 season.

ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi reported Thursday that "while team sources indicated that Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced the Browns to consider Watson the long-term answer, Cleveland's surprising start has shifted the conversation inside the building to whether the 31-year-old passer and the Browns can build short-term momentum."

Oyefusi added, "Team sources said Watson's ability to move past negative plays and stretches instead of compounding them has stood out."

The Biggest Disappointments of NFL Season So Far ☹️

Following a season-opening loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, Watson has led the Browns to back-to-back victories at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and against the visiting Carolina Panthers.

That marked Watson's first time since 2023 winning consecutive games in Cleveland, where in 2022 he signed a fully-guaranteed five-year, $230 million deal for which he has been mostly unavailable.

Watson made his return for the last year of that contract, and the first time since tearing his Achilles tendon in 2024, after beating out Shedeur Sanders for the Week 1 starting job in training camp.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported after the season-opening loss to the Jaguars the Browns planned to re-evaluate the QB1 position after Week 2.

The Browns turned again to Watson as starter for Week 3, after which Rapoport reported on NFL Network Watson had played well enough the Browns no longer wanted to "go week-to-week" in terms of which quarterback would be starting.

Sanders still looks set to stick around in Cleveland, especially given the status of Watson's expiring contract. Cleveland.com's Mary Kay Cabot reported last weekend the Browns have no plans to trade either Sanders or Dillon Gabriel by the Nov. 10 deadline.

With Gabriel currently on IR with a back injury, Sanders will be slated to back up Watson Thursday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Watson is heading into the matchup having so far completed 68.3 percent of his passes for 587 yards with five touchdowns and an interception to go along with 105 rushing yards in three games.

articles.title: Terrell Owens Claps Back at Cris Carter, Deion Sanders Weighs In as Video, Comments Go Viral
articles.summary: Never one to shy away from a discussion, Terrell Owens has put himself in a social media battle with Cris Carter relating back to comments the latter made after a playoff game from January 1998.
articles.body:
Never one to shy away from a discussion, Terrell Owens has put himself in a social media battle with Cris Carter relating back to comments the latter made after a playoff game from January 1998.

On the latest episode of his Fully Loaded podcast, Carter said he "hasn't missed out" on anything by not talking to Owens in response to Owens saying he "can't stand" the Minnesota Vikings legend.

That prompted Owens to clap back in a post on X by quote tweeting the video of Carter's comments and writing he hasn't "missed out on anything not talking to you either."

Their bickering caught the attention of Colorado head coach Deion Sanders, who had plenty of experience from his playing days going up against both Owens and Carter, and urged them to "replace the hate with Love & respect" toward each other.

The origin of the situation appears to stem from Owens recounting a story in which a reporter told him after a Vikings playoff game against the San Francisco 49ers in January 1998 that Carter said Minnesota's cornerbacks "made a mediocre receiver look like a Pro Bowler."

It's not clear which 49ers receiver Carter was said to be describing as mediocre. J.J. Stokes was the one who led the team in receiving yards with 101 in the game. Owens, who was in his second NFL season at that point, had four catches for 49 yards and one touchdown.

San Francisco won the game 38-22 to advance to the NFC Championship Game.

articles.title: Steelers vs. Browns 'Thursday Night Football' betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper break downs his favorite bets in the Steelers-Browns matchup on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
Two of the four teams currently tied for first place in the AFC North square off Thursday night when the Cleveland Browns host the Pittsburgh Steelers at Huntington Bank Field.

The Steelers (2-1) enter this prime-time showdown fresh off a thrilling 30-27 victory against Cincinnati . Down 27-24 in the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh used a pair of Chris Boswell field goals to pull out the home win against quarterback Joe Burrow and the previously unbeaten Bengals .

On the other side, many fans and pundits alike might be a little surprised by Cleveland's 2-1 start to its campaign. After a humbling 34-10 road loss against Jacksonville in the season opener, the Browns have reeled off close victories against Tampa Bay and Carolina . The highlight in the latter win came via a late Harold Fannin Jr. touchdown — his second of the game — to vault Cleveland to the home triumph.

Let's take a deeper look at this intriguing matchup and see where we've located some betting value.

Pittsburgh Steelers (-3, 38.5) at Cleveland Browns

This number hasn't moved much, with Pittsburgh opening as a 2.5-point road favorite. While some books have held spread at that number, others have seen it tick up and moved it to Steelers -3.

In contrast, the total has dropped from an opening number of 40.5 to 38.5 in a contest taking place on a short week. You can even find a few totals of 38 out there at various shops.

Looking more closely at this clash, it's extremely hard to not like the Browns getting the points.

And the data and history surrounding the hosts are the reasons why:

Cleveland is 10-2 straight up at home on Thursday

The Browns are 9-3 against the spread, including covering the number in nine consecutive games

Throw in the fact that Pittsburgh is 0-4 on Thursday nights in Cleveland dating back to 2009 and scored a combined 49 points in those losses and you have the Browns in an ideal historical situation.

I'm backing Cleveland to cover the spread in a spot where they've consistently done well. And I don't think it's out of the question that Deshaun Watson could lead the Browns to an outright victory.

TE Darnell Washington alt receiving yards: 15+ yards (-138) | 20+ yards (+118) | 25+ yards (+178) | 30+ yards (+250) at FanDuel

If there's one area the Cleveland defense has struggled so far this season, it has been covering opposing tight ends.

Case in point came in last week's win against Carolina, where the visiting triumvirate of Darren Waller , Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined for 11 receptions and 128 yards. None of those guys are as imposing as Washington, who's 6-foot-7 and weighs close to 270 pounds.

Washington has also seemed to gain favor with Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers . He finished with a snap share edge over veteran Pat Freiermuth (76%-60%) against the Bengals, hauling in three catches for 67 yards in Week 3.

With that in mind, we're going after this Washington ladder play. He has recorded at least 19 yards receiving in the first three games of the season and I think Rodgers gets this mountain of a man involved early and often against the Browns.

RB Raheim Sanders alt receiving yards: 15+ yards (+126) | 20+ yards (+198) | 25+ yards (+290) | 30+ yards (+410, FanDuel)

We went digging in the weeds for another ladder play and loved what we uncovered tied to Sanders.

With Dylan Sampson parked on the IR, Sanders has established himself as the No. 2 running back behind Quinshon Judkins . And he's the clear passing-down back in this Cleveland offense.

Sanders was quite active against Carolina, running 17 routes. He was targeted five times, finishing with four receptions for 34 yards.

Pittsburgh's pass-rushers have been getting after the opposition's quarterbacks, racking up 8.0 sacks in the first three games. That means Watson is going to have to get the ball out fast and one of the guys most likely to benefit is Sanders.

If you're looking for something more conservative, his line to clear 10 receiving yards sits at -148 at FanDuel. However, I'm going with this ladder angle and hoping Sanders can break off a couple of big plays to clear them all.

A season ago, Fannin led the Cleveland offense with 72 receptions.

Now, three games into the latest campaign, he is on pace to eclipse that number after a sizzling start. Fannin has recorded 14 receptions on 18 targets for 128 yards, highlighted by his seven-catch, 51-yard effort against the Panthers that resulted in two touchdowns.

In my opinion, Fannin is quietly turning into a potential top-five tight end in the league and has clearly become one of Watson's favorite targets in the clutch. And now Cleveland faces a Pittsburgh defense that has struggled to keep opposing tight ends in check.

Through three games, the Pittsburgh defense has conceded 12 yards per reception and a 71.4% catch rate to tight ends. That's just not good enough, especially facing a guy as athletic and dominant as Fannin.

At this price, I'm finding it hard to not back one of Watson's favorite targets to hit paydirt.

articles.body:
Caleb Williams has not missed a game since the Chicago Bears selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. However, an unfortunate hamstring injury has now put the quarterback's availability in question, while head coach Ben Johnson has remained cautious and somewhat vague when discussing the status of his star signal-caller.

The Bears are set to host the New York Jets in Week 4. According to Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic, Williams will not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough , Johnson confirmed, though the coach noted that the quarterback is "getting better every single day." Fishbain also reported that the Bears have not made a decision regarding their starting quarterback.

Williams suffered a non-contact hamstring injury while scrambling during the fourth quarter of Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The injury forced him to leave the field on a cart and immediately raised concerns about his availability moving forward.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Medical evaluations later confirmed that Williams suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain. He was subsequently ruled out for Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles , ending the first stretch of his NFL career in which he had started 36 consecutive regular-season games.

Before the injury, Williams had also become the first Bears quarterback to start every game in consecutive seasons since the NFL expanded to a 16-game schedule in 1978.

Doctors initially projected a recovery period of approximately three to four weeks, putting Williams' potential return around the middle of October. That timeline means the Bears are likely to remain cautious as they determine when their franchise quarterback is ready to return.

Before suffering the injury, Williams had gotten off to a promising start under Johnson. Across his first two starts, he completed 32 of 55 pass attempts for 407 yards, two passing touchdowns, and one interception.

However, for now, his status remains a week-to-week situation as the Bears' medical staff continues monitoring his recovery and progress toward a full return.

articles.title: Should the Raiders trade for Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr.?
articles.summary: Should the Las Vegas Raiders trade for Arizona Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr.?
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are off to a dreamy 3-0 start . Everything is currently firing on all cylinders. Veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins is managing the offense while rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza sits and learns behind the scenes.

One of the Raiders' priorities will be to acquire a true No. 1 receiver for Mendoza. With the Raiders at 3-0, could GM John Spytek consider making a deal near the trade deadline?

The young Raiders will be careful with giving up future picks, as they are still a rebuilding squad despite the 3-0 start. One opportunity that could be worth exploring resides in the NFC. Are the Arizona Cardinals willing to trade underperforming wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.?

Billed as an elite prospect coming out of Ohio State, Harrison has come nowhere near meeting the predraft hype. The fourth overall selection in 2024 seriously regressed last season as a sophomore compared to his rookie year. This season, he's registered four receptions and zero touchdowns in three appearances.

The Raiders recently lost Jack Bech for an undetermined amount of time due to a serious forearm injury. Bech has been placed on IR . His injury makes a thin Raiders depth chart at receiver even thinner.

With a decision needed this coming offseason on his fifth-year option, the rebuilding Cardinals could be looking to trade Harrison. Trade activity is starting to pick up around the league, with the Pittsburgh Steelers sending cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday evening. The Raiders should at least explore what it'd take to acquire Harrison and give him a much-needed fresh start.

articles.title: NFL Legend Kurt Warner Posts Tutorial Video for Young QBs
articles.summary: Kurt Warner is once again using his experience to help the next generation of quarterbacks avoid one of the most common mistakes in the passing game. The for...
articles.body:
Kurt Warner is once again using his experience to help the next generation of quarterbacks avoid one of the most common mistakes in the passing game. The former NFL quarterback recently shared a tutorial explaining how young QBs can improve their execution on double-move routes.

Warner's lesson focuses on what quarterbacks should do after initially looking toward the receiver during the route. Instead of keeping their eyes locked on the wideout after recognizing that he has created separation, quarterbacks should quickly check the free safety or return their vision to the middle of the field before resetting their feet.

That brief adjustment can make a major difference in the timing of the throw. When a receiver executes a double move, he still needs time to complete the route and regain his full speed, meaning a quarterback who rushes the throw can release the ball before his target is ready to accelerate downfield.

The former NFL star also explained how quarterbacks can fall into the trap of watching a receiver for too long after seeing him win the route. While the initial reaction may be to deliver the ball immediately, keeping the eyes on the receiver can cause the quarterback to rush his mechanics and ultimately miss a potential explosive play.

NFL Icon Kurt Warner Shares Tutorial Video for Young Quarterbacks

Warner recently shared a video that'll help young quarterbacks improve their game and do away with their mistakes . This can be seen in a post he made on X.

Resetting the feet while briefly looking away gives the receiver an opportunity to finish the route before the quarterback returns his attention to the target. Once the quarterback looks back, he can better judge the receiver's speed and position, allowing him to make a more accurate throw and maximize the opportunity created by the route.

Warner's tutorial offers a simple reminder that successful quarterback play often depends on small technical details. For young passers and coaches looking to improve, mastering footwork, eye discipline and timing on double moves could turn missed opportunities into some of the biggest plays on the field.

articles.title: The NFL May Be Approaching the Breaking Point of the 17-Game Season
articles.summary: When the league expanded the schedule in 2021, it went from 16 to 17 games came with one fewer preseason game. Five years later, it is fair to wonder whether...
articles.body:
What it may not have fully accounted for was everything that comes with asking the same basic roster to survive a 17-game season.

When the league expanded the schedule in 2021, it made the first change to the regular season since 1978. The move from 16 to 17 games came with one fewer preseason game, but the basic structure of an NFL roster remained largely familiar. Teams still build around a 53-man roster and, under current rules, generally dress 47 or 48 players on game day.

Five years later, it is fair to wonder whether the 17-game season has outgrown the roster designed to survive it.

One additional game doesn't sound dramatic.

It is only 60 more minutes of football, after all. Except it isn't.

Another game means another week of practice, another week of players managing existing injuries, another round of collisions, and another opportunity for something that was merely sore in September to become something far more significant by December.

The postseason makes the equation even more demanding. A team reaching the Super Bowl can play as many as 21 combined regular-season and playoff games. That is a long way from the NFL schedule players once navigated.

The league partially compensated for the 17-game season by reducing the preseason from four games to three. That limits some unnecessary August exposure, particularly for established starters. But preseason snaps and regular-season snaps aren't interchangeable.

The 17th game is different from the preseason game that disappeared when the NFL expanded the schedule. Nobody is protecting starters in Week 18 because the result doesn't count. For some teams, that game decides whether there will even be a Week 19.

The 17-Game Season Has Put More Pressure on 53 Players

The NFL didn't suddenly become an injury-plagued sport when the schedule expanded. That's too easy an argument to make, and probably the wrong one.

Look instead at what happens to the bottom half of a roster over four months.

An offensive lineman who was signed to play guard may end up at center. The swing tackle gets thrown into the lineup. A defensive back gets promoted from the practice squad on Saturday and is covering kicks on Sunday. By late in the year, teams are signing players who weren't part of the original plan at all.

Some of that happened when there were 16 games, too. The difference with a 17-game season is that there is now another week to get through before the playoffs even begin.

And 53 isn't really 53 on Sunday. The game-day limit leaves coaches with 47 or 48 active players. Take out the specialists, backup quarterback, and players whose primary jobs are on special teams, and the available depth gets eaten up quickly.

That's one reason offensive line versatility has become so valuable. A reserve who can play center and both guard spots solves more problems than a player who can only do one thing. It isn't necessarily because he's the better player. Sometimes he's simply the player a 53-man roster makes easier to keep.

The 17-game season gives teams one more week for those compromises to catch up with them.

The 17-Game Season Could Change the Value of a Backup

Maybe the bigger adjustment needs to happen before anybody gets hurt.

NFL teams have already done this with defensive linemen. They rotate. A starting defensive tackle doesn't need to play every snap. Nobody looks at 45 snaps instead of 65 and assumes he's been demoted.

Teams decided a fresh defensive lineman can be more useful than squeezing every possible snap out of the starter.

Running backs have gone through something similar. The days when every team wanted one back, carrying the ball 350 times, are mostly gone.

That thinking is harder to apply elsewhere.

Nobody is voluntarily sitting a healthy left tackle for two series in a close game. Quarterbacks certainly aren't rotating. If a receiver is clearly better than the guy behind him, coaches want him on the field.

That's understandable. Coaches aren't paid to have the healthiest roster in January. They have to win the game in front of them first.

But over a 17-game season, those snaps add up.

At some point, having a capable second player at a position may need to become more than protection against an injury. It may become part of how teams get through the year.

There is a problem with saying the NFL should simply expand rosters.

Five more players mean five more salaries.

Unless the salary cap changes with the roster limit, teams would still be working with the same pool of money. A bigger roster filled with minimum-salary players doesn't automatically solve a depth problem.

There are other ways the league could approach it.

Additional roster spots could be treated differently against the cap. Injured reserve rules could become more forgiving for shorter-term injuries. The NFL could expand the number of players available on game day without making a dramatic change to the 53-man roster.

A second bye week deserves to be part of the discussion, too.

There probably isn't one fix because there isn't one problem. Teams need enough players, enough money to keep those players, and enough recovery time to make the whole thing useful.

The 17-game season has been around long enough that it already feels normal. An 18th game wouldn't feel normal immediately.

That would potentially put a Super Bowl team on the field 22 times between the regular season and postseason. Think about that from the perspective of an offensive lineman who rarely leaves the field.

That's a lot of snaps before even counting practices.

If the NFL eventually goes there, adding another bye would make sense. So would another look at roster limits.

The league could also force teams to adjust naturally. Coaches might become more willing to rotate players. General managers might spend differently, putting more money into the 30th through 45th players on the roster instead of concentrating so much of it at the top.

But there is a reason that hasn't happened already.

A coach isn't going to take his best tackle off the field in a three-point game because he might need him four months later. That's a nice idea until the backup gives up a sack and the team loses.

The NFL created a longer season, but coaches still have to survive it one Sunday at a time.

The 17-Game Season Isn't Going Back to 16

Another regular-season game means another weekend people watch football. It means another home game every other year for each team. It means another television window the NFL can sell.

Sixteen games aren't coming back. We will have a 17-game season for the foreseeable future.

So the interesting discussion isn't whether the league should undo the 17-game season. It's whether everything surrounding the schedule should continue operating the same way.

The NFL has changed plenty in the name of player safety. Rules have changed. Equipment has improved. Practice time has been reduced and regulated.

Maybe roster size and rest eventually belong on that list. No rule is going to keep every player healthy. Neither will five additional roster spots, nor another bye week. Football doesn't work that way.

But there's a big gap between eliminating injuries and giving teams a better chance of handling them. Right now, too many seasons eventually become a test of who still has enough healthy players left.

Maybe the 17-game season isn't actually too long. Maybe 53 players aren't enough for it. That's a different argument, and it becomes a much bigger one if the NFL ever adds an 18th game.

The league doesn't need to tear up its entire roster system. A few more spots could help. So could another bye, different injured reserve rules, or more flexibility with the players available on Sundays.

There will always be attrition in football. Nobody is changing that.

But the NFL changed the length of its season five years ago from 16 games to a 17-game season. Eventually, it may have to change the roster built to play it.

articles.title: Grading Joey Porter Jr. Blockbuster NFL Trade Between Cowboys and Steelers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have established a trade pipeline with the Dallas Cowboys. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will reunite with former Steelers teammates Broderick Jones, whom Dallas acquired about a month ago, and George Pickens.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have established a trade pipeline with the Dallas Cowboys. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. will reunite with former Steelers teammates Broderick Jones, whom Dallas acquired about a month ago, and George Pickens.

According to ESPN's Todd Archer and Brooke Pryor , Dallas sent Pittsburgh a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for Porter.

Porter has dealt with a back injury, and not so coincidentally, a contract dispute since training camp.

Early in July, Chris Mack of the Kaboly and Mack podcast said there's a "belief" that Porter wanted an extension averaging around $30 million. That sounds reasonable, given that cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Devon Witherspoon, who also entered the league in 2023, signed new deals averaging $33.75 million and $33 million, respectively.

Instead of giving Porter an extension, Pittsburgh dealt him, which is a move many saw coming because of how the franchise does business.

So, let's break down the short- and long-term layers of this trade to assess these teams' defensive outlook and Porter's future. Here are the immediate grades.

The Dallas Cowboys left Rio de Janeiro embarrassed, having allowed a 27-yard completion and a game-winning 56-yard field goal to the Baltimore Ravens in just seven seconds. While you can blame defensive coordinator Christian Parker for a poor play call after the touchback, the Cowboys absolutely need a lead cornerback.

Dallas has allowed seven passing touchdowns in three weeks. Cornerback DaRon Bland is allowing a passer rating of 108.8 in coverage. Cobie Durant didn't suit up last week because of a hamstring injury.

When Joey Porter Jr. is ready to take the field, he'll be the Cowboys' clear-cut No. 1 cover man on the boundary. Through three seasons in Pittsburgh, he recorded 31 pass breakups, three interceptions and allowed a 57.2 passer rating in coverage. Touted for his man coverage ability out of Penn State, he can shadow lead wide receivers and force quarterbacks to target secondary pass-catchers.

Dallas should be far better in pass coverage going forward, as long as Porter's supposed back injury clears up.

Beyond a significant upgrade at cornerback, the Cowboys didn't even give up a premium 2027 draft pick, which is a major plus with all the buzz around potential first- and second-round prospects.

Lastly, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , Dallas isn't expected to sign Porter to a new deal, which was a sticking point in the cornerback's divorce from the Steelers.

The Cowboys get an established and ascending player, keep their top 2027 picks and won't go through the headache of contract negotiations, which contributed to Porter's recent inactivity in Pittsburgh. This is a slam dunk move for Dallas' front office.

As some may know, the Steelers are notoriously stingy with guaranteed money, and they don't negotiate with players during the regular season.

While Steelers general managers before Omar Khan have abided by these guidelines, The Athletic's Mike DeFabo pointed the finger at him anyway.

" While most of the public criticism has been pointed at Porter, the Steelers should not be absolved of blame. Khan has a history of letting negotiations linger to the last minute . That comes along with two long-standing (and, arguably, outdated) front-office policies: The Steelers rarely give out guaranteed money and they don't negotiate contracts during the season."

With $11.6 million in cap space and projected to be $9.2 million over the limit in 2027, Pittsburgh has to be conservative with contracts, but this isn't the one.

The Steelers have a veteran-led roster with 42-year-old quarterback Aaron Rodgers and several defensive players like T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward and Jalen Ramsey in their 30s. Khan has a win-now squad that needs young talent to stay competitive long term.

On the one hand, the Steelers signed defensive lineman Keeanu Benton, outside linebacker Nick Herbig, wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr., running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Darnell Washington to extensions. They're all up-and-coming talent or in their prime.

Yet, Khan couldn't make room on the books for the team's top cornerback. Barring an unreasonable contract request, the Steelers should've prioritized Porter's deal over the players they extended this offseason.

To make matters worse, the Steelers didn't get a player in return who plays the same position as Porter or a pick that's likely to help them within the next year. Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. could be a decent cornerback duo, but the former has missed 12 games since 2023 and the latter has allowed two touchdowns and a passer rating of 135.4 so far this season.

In the short term, this is a major blunder for the Steelers .

Porter may benefit from a change of scenery. The Cowboys have a more potent offense than the Steelers' 26th-ranked scoring unit. So his defensive contributions may stand out more when opponents force the ball downfield while playing from behind. Dallas is also less likely to waste a solid defensive outing with a low-scoring output.

However, Porter may be in the same contract situation he was in Pittsburgh.

As previously noted, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Porter will play out the season on his current deal.

So, does Porter's back injury clear up quickly as he bets on himself, hoping Dallas rewards him in the next offseason? Did he just want a split from the Steelers, knowing that the Cowboys weren't going to sign him to an immediate extension either?

In a contract year, Porter didn't get what he wanted and still has to prove himself worthy of a lucrative deal that puts him on a similar pay scale as cornerbacks Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez. And there's no guarantee that the Cowboys will extend him. Like George Pickens this year, they could franchise-tag him.

Perhaps Porter's contract negotiations with the Steelers soured their relationship beyond repair, and he preferred to chase a new deal elsewhere. Still, this isn't the best possible outcome for a player who held out for a new deal.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin shows off incredibly detailed Minecraft city he built when he was coaching Steelers
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin put a lot of thought into lighting and interior design... really.
articles.body:
For all his success, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin received his fair share of criticism during his 19-year run in the position. But one thing he could never be condemned for was his attention to detail, a trait that apparently extends far beyond his football life.

Turns out, while Tomlin was leading the Steelers to winning records he was also building an elaborately detailed city in the video game Minecraft. Tomlin revealed that tidbit during a September interview on the "Today Show," saying he spent 12 years planning and building the city.

It seemed too outlandish to be true. Was a future Hall of Fame coach spending his down time painstakingly building a city in a video game popular with a much younger generation?

Well, Tomlin gave fans that answer Wednesday night with a tour of his elaborate city. It was … pretty incredible.

Prior to showing off his city, Tomlin revealed that he started playing Minecraft as a way to connect with his kids. Even though his kids have left the game behind, Tomlin has continued to add to his city. During his interview with the "Today Show," Tomlin said his kids — who are grown now — encourage him to show off the city every time they visit.

And if the above clip is any indication, they had many, many reasons to encourage their dad to make his interest public. Tomlin clearly put a lot of thought and care into the project, explaining that he wanted to build the city around a large body of water.

From there, he kept making additions … like, lots of them. Tomlin showed off therapy rooms, public restrooms, a baseball stadium and glass elevators, among many, many other details . Tomlin also gave his thoughts on interior decorating, lighting fixtures and bedroom furniture in his video. No, really.

Tomlin's full video — which he posted on his YouTube page — came in under 20 minutes, which was nowhere near enough time for him to show off his entire city. Fans hoping to see more are in luck, though. Tomlin teased future episodes in which he planned to show off other aspects of his city.

Now that he's no longer coaching, Tomlin presumably has even more time to keep adding to his Minecraft city. While many assumed Tomlin's time away from the NFL would be short-lived, Wednesday's unveiling may have paved the way for Tomlin to turn in a lucrative second act as one of the biggest Minecraft streamers around. That sounds a lot less stressful than taking on another head-coaching job in the NFL, especially for someone already as accomplished as Tomlin.

articles.title: Brian Burns Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Giants Star's Knee, Return Timeline Ahead of Surgery
articles.summary: It appears that New York Giants star edge rusher Brian Burns could be sidelined for longer than initially expected.
articles.body:
It appears that New York Giants star edge rusher Brian Burns could be sidelined for longer than initially expected.

After Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed that Burns suffered a torn ACL in Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans, league and team sources told The Athletic's Dan Duggan that he also tore the lateral meniscus in his right knee. The 28-year-old is scheduled to undergo surgery to repair both injuries on Thursday.

Duggan noted that the "typical timeline for recovery from ACL and meniscus surgery is 9-to-12 months." Giants star receiver Malik Nabers suffered a similar injury early in the 2025 season and had to undergo a second "clean-up" surgery to remove scar tissue, but he recovered in time to start the 2026 campaign.

Before Sunday's injury, Burns had been a shining example of consistency. In his first seven NFL seasons between the Giants and the Carolina Panthers, he had missed just three games.

A three-time Pro Bowler, Burns is New York's defensive leader. His injury came just a week after the team lost second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart to season-ending knee surgery. Harbaugh explained the team's mindset after these devastating injuries.

"We got our quarterback one week and probably our top defensive player, you might say, the next week is shocking," Harbaugh told reporters on Monday. "But you've got to overcome the shock, and you've got to get ready to play the next game and find a way to win the next game. That's what we'll be doing as a team. But I feel bad for Brian more than anything, my heart breaks for him that way."

It can be expected that edge rusher Kaybon Thibodeaux will see an increased role opposite Abdul Carter in Burns' absence. The Giants have produced just one sack this season, ranking 31st in the league.

New York (2-1) will try to get used to life without Burns when it faces the Arizona Cardinals (1-2) in Week 4.

articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers finally found some rhythm. Now comes the place where the Pittsburgh Steelers have repeatedly lost theirs.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers finally found some rhythm. Now comes the place where the Pittsburgh Steelers have repeatedly lost theirs.Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals. On Thursday, he faces Deshaun Watson and a Cleveland Browns team carrying history firmly on its side. The Steelers have not won in Cleveland since 2021, and their Thursday record against the Browns is even worse.Why has Cleveland been such a problem for the Steelers on Thursday Night Football?Pittsburgh has lost all four of its Thursday games against Cleveland, according to an Oct. 1 report from Ryan Pawloski. The Steelers have also gone 3-6-1 across their last 10 games in Cleveland.The Browns have built the opposite reputation on Thursdays.Cleveland owns an 11-2 record in Thursday Night Football games and has won nine straight Thursday contests. That history creates a strange setup for a Pittsburgh team coming off one of its better offensive performances of the young season.There is one major variable the Steelers did not have during those previous trips: Mike McCarthy.Pawloski reported that McCarthy has gone 17-8 in Thursday games during his coaching career. His teams have also won each of their last six Thursday appearances.That does not erase Pittsburgh's problems in Cleveland, but it gives the Steelers a coach with a strong record on short weeks.McCarthy also enters the matchup after Pittsburgh's offense showed tangible improvement against Cincinnati. Rodgers moved the ball through the air, while the offensive line produced a stronger showing after two new players entered the lineup.The Steelers will need that progress to carry over quickly. Cleveland has given them little room for error in this setting.Can Aaron Rodgers beat the Browns’ pass rush if Cleveland forces him to play even faster?The Browns know Rodgers' quickest weapon might be the one that never appears in a box score: how fast he gets rid of the football.Browns defensive lineman Jared Verse addressed that problem before Thursday's game. articles.title: Week 4 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Raiders ready for their biggest game in Las Vegas vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The Chiefs and Raiders are both 3-0 heading into a big AFC West game.
articles.body:
When Patrick Mahomes starts at quarterback, the Kansas City Chiefs are 13-2 against the Las Vegas Raiders . But the Raiders have changed.

It's hard to get used to the idea of the Raiders being good. They've been bad for so long that it's strange to think of them any other way, unless you're still watching old clips of Ken Stabler or Marcus Allen. However, there is no evidence that their 3-0 start is fraudulent. Even if there was some trepidation about getting behind the Raiders' 2-0 start, a 35-27 comeback win at New Orleans was pretty impressive.

The Raiders are ninth in DVOA , ranking 13th in offense, ninth in defense and fifth in special teams. They're 15th in EPA per play on offense and second in EPA per play allowed. There's a new coaching staff, the roster has been remade, and the early results are impressive.

The Chiefs are good, too, of course. Any worry about Mahomes being rusty coming off ACL surgery has faded away during a 3-0 start. The Chiefs aren't going anywhere.

But this is the biggest game the Raiders have had since moving to Las Vegas . Not that the Chiefs won't be ready, but this should have a playoff feel at Allegiant Stadium. It has been a long time since the Raiders could feel this confident in what they're building. Las Vegas is a sound football team and even if they lose to a strong Chiefs team, it seems unlikely they'll be blown out. Raiders +4.5 i s the pick. It's time to find out how good they might be this season.

Here are the rest of my picks against the spread for Week 4 of the NFL season:

These are two flawed 2-1 teams. The Steelers had one offensive touchdown through two weeks before a good game against the Bengals last week. The Browns are 31st in the NFL in EPA per rushing play and Deshaun Watson is averaging fewer than 200 passing yards per game. But someone is going to be 3-1 unless there's a tie, which might be fitting. Cleveland is at home on a short week getting a field goal, and they're somehow 11-1 in home Thursday night games, according to longtime Browns reporter Tony Grossi . They're the tepid pick.

The NFL's Sunday window opens early. Set your alarm for the first 9:30 a.m. Eastern start of the year, from London. There should be plenty of scoring in this one. The Colts had the worst defense in the NFL through two weeks (though it played well last week vs. Houston ) and the Commanders are 31st in the NFL in points allowed. London games are usually a bit odd, and the Commanders can score even with Marcus Mariota at QB if Jayden Daniels doesn't return. I'll take the points.

The Eagles are 2-1, but Monday night exposed them. They were dominated by the Bears. The first two games, they barely beat Washington and Tennessee , and now those middling performances look even worse after they got blasted in Chicago . We can say the Rams are 1-2, but are probably a bad defensive pass interference call away from being 2-1 with the one loss being the weird game in Australia. I have much more faith in them than Philadelphia .

It is frightening to pick an 0-3 Buccaneers team with an undrafted rookie quarterback. But teams this season who are starting a QB other than their Week 1 starter are 6-0 this season, according to Josh Dubow of Associated Press . And it's very hard to pick the Packers as a road favorite. They have been awful this season. Can Bucs rookie QB Jalon Daniels just do enough to keep the Bucs close? We'll find out.

Maybe what we saw Monday night was the typical bump a team can get from its first game with a backup quarterback. But the Bears looked good with Case Keenum , and it's fair to credit Ben Johnson's coaching for that. The Jets could be without Breece Hall , Mason Taylor and Adonai Mitchell , three key skill-position players. New York hasn't been that bad, but here's a pick for the coaching matchup.

The Patriots are another team that is hard to pick. They look bad. This also feels like a playoff game for them, even though it's only Week 4. If they fall to 1-3, three games behind the Bills, the chances of winning the division get very slim. If the Patriots have any hope at all of being a factor this season, you'll see it on Sunday.

It's possible Jacksonville is the team we're not talking about enough. The Jaguars had one bad half against the Broncos . In the other five halves this season, the Jaguars have outscored their three opponents 79-19. The Bengals have looked pretty good to start the season as well, though a defensive letdown last week was disappointing. We might start talking more about the Jaguars after Week 4.

It's hard to come up with a logical argument for the Titans, but bad teams cover the spread often in the NFL. If you play survivor, you understand this. Also, the Ravens are coming straight off a trip to Brazil. The Titans need any edge they can get.

I refuse to give up on the Texans. It looks like they'll have Nico Collins back this week, which the offense desperately needs. Also, like the Ravens, the Cowboys are coming straight back from Brazil, and unlike Baltimore they're playing on the road. The Cowboys also had a miserable loss last week that will be hard to shake off. This is the last time we're picking Houston if it loses this week. Maybe. We'll see.

Arizona has been pretty good. Still, it's surprising to see the Cardinals as a road favorite. We know why. The Giants offense isn't going to be fun to watch with Jameis Winston (spoiler alert: It's unlikely to be any better with J.J. McCarthy , if and when he gets his shot). But this line seems very disrespectful to a 2-1 Giants team that will play hard and is well-coached. Also, it's a team coming from the West to play one of those early East Coast starts.

The Dolphins will cover a spread this season. Nobody goes 0-17 against the spread. I'm not sure it's this week though. The matchup of Brian Flores' Vikings defense against a Dolphins offense now without De'Von Achane seems treacherous. If Justin Jefferson doesn't play that does give the Dolphins a shot to keep it close. But it's too hard to take Miami right now.

Are the 49ers the product of an easy schedule? Perhaps to some extent. The Rams had jet lag and the Dolphins and Cardinals aren't very good. But the 49ers have handled business and Brock Purdy is red hot. They've played better than every other team so far this season. The Broncos aren't a bad team, but the first halves (they've been a no-show in the first half for all three games) is a real problem. I'll go with the NFL's hottest team and hope they take on no more injuries before kickoff.

The last time Jim Harbaugh had a losing season, not counting a truncated 2020 season, was 2008 at Stanford. This season could break that streak, though. The Chargers have been legitimately awful. Even a +4 turnover margin at Buffalo didn't lead to a win, or even covering a 7-point spread. And now they get a Seattle team coming off a loss. But there's no way the Chargers can be this bad all season. Right?

The Lions will score points. That seems like a safe prediction. The Panthers have played one decent offense this season and gave up 59 points to Chicago. This week they put both starting cornerbacks, Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson , on injured reserve. Detroit is going to move the ball. Carolina can too. The Lions' defense is bad. But the Panthers' offensive line injuries are piling up. They're without both tackles and guard Damien Lewis is set to miss time, too, which helps the Lions. It's hard to trust Detroit's defense, but I think the Lions might score at will.

This isn't the best Monday night game, but it is interesting. Are the Falcons suddenly good now that they have competent quarterback play from Michael Penix Jr.? What do we make of the Saints? They are 1-2, but also won at Baltimore and nearly won at Detroit. I believe the Saints are the best team in that division, and what we saw from the Falcons in Week 3 says more about the Packers than Atlanta .

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' legendary secret language: How the Steelers' Google Doc of roughly 75 hand signals sets bar for NFL cat-and-mouse game
articles.summary: Yahoo Sports canvassed 17 players and 10 coaches across 11 NFL teams to better understand the chess game of hand signals for Rodgers and beyond. Their perspe...
articles.body:
LATROBE, Pa. — On the first day of Pittsburgh Steelers training camp last year, Aaron Rodgers sat down with quarterback Will Howard .

Rodgers' intent: Initiate the rookie as the latest NFL backup quarterback to manage his starter's hand signals.

"He gave me kind of the baseline of like, 'All right, hitch, slant, routes, a couple of combinations here and there, some formation signals …'" Howard told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "We would kind of evolve it as we went. So it started off with probably 25, 30 signals and then it ended up being like 75 by the end of [the season]."

Most NFL teams in today's game use far fewer than 75 signals at the line of scrimmage during a season, coaches and players say. But most NFL quarterbacks are not Rodgers. No other active quarterback has his deep trove of 260 regular-season starts. No other active quarterback owns four MVP honors.

So as Rodgers' mental bank of the game grows, so too do his signals evolve in concert. Teammates know "you better be tuned in," Steelers receiver Ben Skowronek told Yahoo Sports, because "in the huddle, it's going to be real brief." Opponents know Rodgers is liable to use more signals — real and dummy — than the quarterbacks they face most other weeks.

In a 30-27 win Sunday over the Cincinnati Bengals , Rodgers prepared for one snap by touching his towel with his right hand before and after beckoning with his left ahead of a first-quarter completion to Roman Wilson . He tapped his helmet, pointed in various directions, balled his left hand into a fist and motioned a semicircle like a steering wheel — all before the first quarter expired.

Then came the left shirt waist touch in the second quarter, the right fist behind his back followed by crossing his wrists out front on the same play in the third. By Rodgers' fourth-quarter fists, points and beckoning gestures, a viewer had reason to wonder: Which were meaningful and which were decoys? Defenders ask themselves that question weekly.

"He's definitely a savant," Ravens cornerback Chidobe Awuzie told Yahoo Sports. "He's looking, he's looking, he's doing this, he's doing that. Giving a little signal here, he's changing his split here, shifting the back out to empty, shifting the back back in. …

"He's keeping that brand of football alive."

Yahoo Sports canvassed 17 players and 10 coaches across 11 NFL teams to better understand the chess game of hand signals played by Rodgers and beyond. Their perspectives revealed a mosaic of strategies employed by offenses looking to control games and defenses looking to neutralize threats.

Rodgers is far from the only one to channel the fading era of line-of-scrimmage masters. But players and coaches agree that the 22nd-year Rodgers' signals have developed a life and lore of their own. The roughly 75 signals the Steelers used last year exceeds the Denver Broncos ' 15-25, Baltimore Ravens' 20-30, and Philadelphia Eagles and Seattle Seahawks ' 50-60 each, per coach and player estimates at each team.

So as the Cleveland Browns host the Steelers and 42-year-old Rodgers on Thursday Night Football, what should they beware?

"What you're seeing from Aaron, I'm sure it looks different than what you saw from Aaron," Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton told Yahoo Sports. "It's that house that keeps expanding in the Hamptons. Now we've got a third bedroom up here for the in-law suite and you're like, 'When did that get built?' 'Well, it just got built a couple summers ago. They wanted to see the ocean.' There's no master plan.

"It's just the house that just keeps going with no government or local restrictions. That's what [his system] looks like."

As QB signals get creative, 'it happens a lot more than people realize'

Not everyone relies on a signals Google Doc like the Steelers do.

The Seahawks last year tracked their signals in a hard-copy notebook, quarterback Drew Lock told Yahoo Sports, as then-offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak also limited weekly game plans to hard copies that were shredded in the corner of the room after each contest. No secrecy measure spared.

The Eagles displayed their signals, which sometimes resulted from Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee Googling sign language, on their meeting room board. But they chose to limit signal usage in training camp so players who were cut and landed on other teams couldn't leak the code to their next team, McKee told Yahoo Sports.

"Pretty much every game there is at least a couple plays [where] nobody really knows, but it means something and it's going to change the whole play," McKee said. "Sometimes it's the obvious ones where you're tapping the helmet and you're yelling out different things and it's a real obvious call. But some of them are pretty discreet.

"I would say it happens a lot more than people realize."

The more a team plays in prime time, the easier it is for opponents to track hand signals and code words given the increase in camera angles and microphones for the broadcast. Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott knows his sleights often land on TV copy, so he switches them.

"There's kind of this base one that I have of like, 'Yeah, this means slant,' but if I've done that too much and put it on film, I'm going to change it up," Prescott told Yahoo Sports. "It's actually a fun kind of back and forth to even create them with the guys. Sometimes, I'm like, 'Hey, I need a word for [this]' and they'll all be thinking.

The most common hand signals across the NFL guide teams through two-minute situations, when up-tempo offenses aim not to huddle and thus need to communicate nonverbally. Single-receiver signals build from there. Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will motion to a receiver whose one-on-one matchup in man coverage dictates a favorable matchup, he said. Single-receiver signals are often more subtle than signals that change an entire play and thus need to reach 10 other players. Film against the Minnesota Vikings , a blitz-happy team with a high-decibel stadium, is likely to show more signal examples, coaches say. Other signals could indicate a quarterback shifting his protection between right and left, or calling for a player to motion.

Potentially telling motions range from pulling on a chin strap and tapping the sides of a helmet to touching the thigh pad or pulling at the waist of a jersey. Points in different directions could mean different things. A butt pat or thumbs up is often notable. The Broncos began with digits zero to 10 after drafting Lock in 2019, he said. Defensive backs study these signals more often than linemen, whose pre-snap stances might cloud their vision. Linemen instead sometimes listen to "bug reports" to guess code words, Broncos edge rusher Zach Allen keeping scouting reports from past years to track play-callers from one stop to the next.

"I'll literally have my wife go through my office and be like, 'Hey, can you find 2020 this because this coordinator was there and see …?" Allen told Yahoo Sports. "I remember [Shane] Steichen when he was in Philly going to Indianapolis , there was a little bit of similar stuff."

Whether signals or code words, a challenge lingers: The same word or motion means plenty at some times and absolutely nothing at others. Defenses relying on their advance scouting have been burned.

"I stopped doing that years ago," Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said of emphasizing signal analysis. "It's like chasing a ghost. And if they're smart, they're going to change those signals. … You spend so much energy on it [then] it never happens and you lose track of the basic stuff."

Energy spent scouting former NFL quarterback Tom Brady 's signals touches a particular sore point across the league.

Joseph remembers a 2012 or 2013 game against the Patriots when Brady was signaling a screen by tapping his foot. Joseph screamed "screen, screen" only for Brady to adjust to a screen-and-go.

Safety Brandon Jones remembers playing in a Dolphins-Buccaneers game when the Dolphins thought they disguised their Cover 3 zone defense by aligning as if in man. Brady wasn't fooled.

"He starts screaming out, 'Cover 3,'" Jones told Yahoo Sports, "and I'm just like, 'OK, this guy's just different."

And 49ers linebacker Fred Warner hasn't forgotten a 2022 signal in which Brady prompted 49ers defenders to gun toward an expected screen. Brady instead threw a go ball to Mike Evans, who raced the remaining 68 yards to the end zone .

An offensive holding penalty nullified the score. But the lesson Warner learned stuck.

"You want to be able to pick up on certain things, but it's just not absolute," Warner told Yahoo Sports. "Whether it's hand signals, formations, personnel, something might be like 99.9. But there's just always a chance that it's just not going to be that in a game setting. …

Defenses adopt Rodgers-specific strategies in hopes they won't 'look like an idiot'

Coaches from three teams that have faced Rodgers since he joined the Steelers were split on how to handle his rotation of signals.

One AFC assistant said they didn't pay attention to Rodgers' signals given how often he changes them. An NFC assistant remembered that when Rodgers pretended to put a belt around his waist with both hands, he was most often calling a screen against blitz looks — except, of course, the times when Rodgers changed that call anticipating defenses would expect the screen. An assistant from a different AFC team noted how Rodgers' signals stand out.

"He signals things really fast," the assistant said, speaking on condition of anonymity due to competitive advantage concerns. "Some of the QBs like to be very demonstrative to make sure it's clear. He is very quick and, what did he actually just do there? I don't know.

"You can't guarantee week to week that the same thing means the same thing because then you bite on it and it's a double move or something. And then you look like an idiot."

So defensive coaches have needed to get creative.

Sure, much of game plans this year focus on Rodgers' dipping athleticism and mobility in his 40s. The New England Patriots in Week 2 capitalized on Rodgers' shoddy protection, pressuring him on 38.6% of dropbacks, per Next Gen Stats. Against the Bengals on Sunday, Rodgers fared better against pressure and threw for two touchdowns of 20+ air yards after failing to complete any of his nine deep pass attempts in the first two weeks.

What do the Browns expect as the Steelers arrive in Cleveland as 2.5-point road favorites?

"He's got an unbelievably quick trigger, I mean, he can just flick it, unbelievably accurate," Browns head coach Todd Monken said. "There's not anything he hasn't seen. When you talk about a student of the game, not only has he seen it, but highly intelligent.

"You have to do a great job with your disguises."

Can defenses fool Rodgers? They're more likely to try in today's NFL than a prior era, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said.

"Because his [football intelligence] is so high, you can do a little bit more from a disguise standpoint to try to mess with him," Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver told Yahoo Sports. "Some of these younger quarterbacks nowadays, you can disguise all you want and they don't care. They're going to find the space, post up and usually it's a lot of predetermined throws.

"With Aaron, you know he's trying to figure it all out."

Meanwhile, Steelers teammates will keep trying to figure out Rodgers' signals. That's proven a stressful task even for later-career veterans like 12th-year receiver Adam Thielen last year and seventh-year Michael Pittman Jr. this year, each said.

Howard led signal meetings for offensive players the morning before game days last year, he said, a common practice around the NFL that ranges from receivers parroting the signals back in a meeting to occasional signal walkthroughs on the field.

Most signals are covered in meetings. But sometimes Rodgers will give a heads-up to one receiver at the line of scrimmage who then tells the next what to expect after the snap, Skowronek said.

"He definitely takes pride in the signals," Skowronek said. "And then sometimes he signals something [in practice] that maybe he used in the past and you're like, 'What the f*** is that, Aaron?'"

When that happens, it's time to return to the Google Doc. Will there be another entry? Or will self-described "signal dictionary" Howard simply remind players of the tried-and-true existing plan?

"It's a lot of signals," Steelers receiver DK Metcalf told Yahoo Sports. "But I mean, they help us win football games at the end of the day when we're all connected."

Jori Epstein is a senior NFL reporter for Yahoo Sports and the author of 'The Upstander: How Surviving the Holocaust Sparked Max Glauben's Mission to Dismantle Hate.' She previously reported for USA TODAY and The Dallas Morning News. Follow Jori on Twitter @JoriEpstein.
