articles.title: Why the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. and what it says about the team now and down the road
articles.summary: It's hard to say the Steelers' roster is better after the Porter trade, but they weren't getting anything from him this season anyway.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers had played the game long enough.

They'd gone along with Joey Porter Jr.'s "back injury." They understood his contract demands and negotiated fairly, even if they didn't agree on his view of his value. They'd even waited three games into the season to see whether a deal could be reached, though the franchise's long-standing policy against negotiating in-season meant the talks that ended around Week 1 were never going to restart. So they moved on, sending him to the Dallas Cowboys for a pair of draft picks .

The Steelers' asking price might have been higher initially, but their return was fairly strong, all things considered .

This was a straight-up business deal, even if there was an emotional element to the negotiations given Porter's family ties to the organization. Sometimes business is just business.

Hometown selection or not, the bottom line is the Steelers didn't see Porter as a $30 million cornerback. They weighed the risk of adding another bloated contract on the defensive side of the ball and concluded that the risk outweighed the potential benefits.

It was a decision they probably had to make. Even if Porter's value — both in financial and draft-pick terms — was not as high as some people wanted to make it.

When the Steelers started getting calls on Porter this summer, their asking price almost certainly was higher — far higher. That's often how these types of things start: throw out an unfair price and see what teams' reactions are.

Were they asking for a first-round pick? That wouldn't be shocking. It also wouldn't surprise anyone if the Steelers had a few teams laugh at that price.

On the one hand, Porter was the first pick of Round 2 (32nd overall) and had played well, starting 41 of 47 games (of a possible 51), defending 31 passes with 3 interceptions. At 26 years old, he's theoretically entering his prime years.

On the other hand, his contract situation lowered his value. Porter was entering the final year of his deal and was asking for elite CB money, reportedly starting at $30 million per year . If the Steelers were balking at this price, it's likely other teams were as well. The general consensus has been that Porter is not in the Devon Witherspoon-Christian Gonzalez tier of cornerbacks, although the real tell will be what Dallas thinks of him whenever that contract extension happens.

When the Steelers couldn't get a first-rounder in return, they likely dropped their asking price to a second-rounder and some change. They got that, but in the 2028 draft, not next year.

In terms of apples-to-apples value, the rule of thumb is that a 2028 second-round pick is roughly worth about a 2027 third-rounder. Even if there might be other factors involved, giving up one year of player value drops the pick value by approximately one round. Throwing in a 2027 sixth-round pick bumps the value up ever so slightly.

Dallas was already giving up the higher of the two 2027 first-rounders in the Quinnen Williams trade, and it had only one pick across Rounds 4 and 5 next year. That likely pushed the Cowboys into offering the 2028 second. Next spring's class is regarded as a talented group at first glance, and potentially top-heavy, which also may have factored into the deal.

Was it a bonanza return? No, but it almost certainly was close to, if not the best, the Steelers were going to get.

How Steelers shape up short term after the trade

It's hard to say the Steelers are better, talent-wise, after the Porter trade. However, the drop-off might not be significant.

The Steelers appear to be in relatively solid shape at corner. The current group is Jalen Ramsey , Jamel Dean , Asante Samuel Jr. , Brandin Echols and 2026 third-rounder Daylen Everette . Ramsey is a jack of all trades, manning multiple roles in the secondary. Dean and Samuel have lined up wide, with Everette also seeing extended snaps in the Week 3 win over the Cincinnati Bengals after Samuel struggled. Echols is more of a depth piece.

Pittsburgh was already paying the short-term price with Porter not playing the first three games. It's painful to help develop a homegrown player and then trade him away in his prime, but the way things were going, it was hard to imagine Porter helping the team this season. The two sides were too dug in.

So in measuring what the Steelers lost in the deal, the "now" price isn't terribly high. The problems they have now are the same ones they've had since Week 1.

If Everette can show something, the Steelers might even raise the value of what they'd received from the position to this point of the season. It also helps that the 2-1 Steelers aren't facing a gauntlet of stacked offenses upcoming. It's a fairly manageable offensive slate through the Week 9 bye, facing the Browns twice, the Alec Pierce-less Colts , the Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers and the Saints , with or without rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson, who's on injured reserve.

But any Steelers trade also must be viewed through the lens of this season and whether this team has any more upside than recent iterations, with Pittsburgh losing in the wild-card round five of the past six seasons and missing the postseason the other year. With Aaron Rodgers in his final season, it is reasonable to suggest that the Steelers have yet to indicate they're making a big short-term push now.

And while the trade doesn't have to be indicative of how the Steelers view their own limitations, you don't often see true Super Bowl contenders trading Porter-caliber talents in-season. The 2014 Seattle Seahawks dealt Percy Harvin in the same season they reached the Super Bowl. The 2016 New England Patriots shipped out Jamie Collins the same season they won the whole thing. There have not been many comparable examples since.

The Steelers know they have a major QB question staring them in the face this offseason. They have Drew Allar and Will Howard as two candidates to potentially replace Rodgers, and now they also have two more draft picks that could be used toward acquiring another option there. That might not have been the impetus for the deal — Porter's contract standoff was — but it could have been the justification in the end.

If they viewed themselves as true contenders, perhaps they would have found a way to make the contract happen. Either way, the Steelers accepted a deal at a reasonable return and made it happen. This did not feel like a team that was pressured into making a trade. Their hand might have been forced by Porter's demands, but their arm doesn't appear to have been twisted in signing off on it.

articles.title: New Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, Trent Williams Injury Updates Ahead of 49ers vs. Broncos
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are dealing with multiple injuries to key players ahead of Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos, and general manager John Lynch provided a host of updates Thursday.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are dealing with multiple injuries to key players ahead of Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos, and general manager John Lynch provided a host of updates Thursday.

According to Lynch, wide receiver Mike Evans is trying to play through a rib injury.

"He is old school in his mindset, and he doesn't want to miss. … Mike will make every attempt, and we'll see where that goes," Lynch said.

As for Nick Bosa, Lynch said he is "doing well" even though "calf injuries are sometimes murky." Offensive lineman Trent Williams had something of a better prognosis, as he may practice Thursday as he deals with a shoulder injury.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan already told reporters Bosa will not play against the Broncos, so Lynch's non-commitment on an exact timeline isn't that surprising.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported on Sept. 25 the pass-rusher was expected to be sidelined for "a few weeks."

It seems like Evans will be back much sooner even though he departed the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals on a cart and never returned. Shanahan told reporters the injury, "shouldn't be long term, and we've got to see how it goes throughout the week."

Having Evans available against the Broncos would be key, as no other wide receiver was credited with a catch during the win over the Cardinals. Instead, quarterback Brock Purdy relied on tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey coming out of the backfield.

The updates on Williams also seem positive even though he exited the Cardinals game in the third quarter and never returned. Vederian Lowe filled in and would likely be called upon again if Williams is out, but the starter is one of the best offensive linemen of his generation and a future Hall of Famer.

Shanahan said Williams "should be good to go by Thursday's [practice]," which Lynch reiterated with his comments.

Despite the injury concerns, the 49ers are 3-0. They will look to continue stacking wins and building momentum against the Broncos and may have both Evans and Williams available.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. willing to play for the Cowboys without a new contract after Steelers standoff; Here’s why
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr.’s contract situation helped push his Pittsburgh Steelers tenure to the breaking point. His arrival in Dallas comes with a surprising twist.
articles.body: Joey Porter Jr.’s contract situation helped push his Pittsburgh Steelers tenure to the breaking point. His arrival in Dallas comes with a surprising twist.The 26-year-old cornerback is reportedly willing to play for the Dallas Cowboys without a new deal in place. That matters because ESPN reported Porter had spent months seeking an extension before Pittsburgh traded him for two future draft picks.Why is Joey Porter Jr. willing to play for the Cowboys without a contract extension?Longtime NFL reporter Ed Werder reported Oct. 1 that a source said Porter is comfortable playing out his current contract in Dallas.The reason appears to be simple. According to Werder, the Cowboys were the team Porter most wanted to join after leaving Pittsburgh.That gives the situation a very different feel from the contract dispute that followed him through the offseason.ESPN reported that Porter and the Steelers had a significant gap in how they valued his next contract. The structure of the proposed deal was also a major issue. Porter missed Pittsburgh’s first three games while dealing with a back injury and remained without the extension he wanted.Eventually, the relationship reached its end.ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Pittsburgh and Porter had essentially reached a point where a long-term agreement was no longer realistic. Porter also wanted out.Dallas offered him a landing spot without solving the contract question immediately.According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, the Cowboys did not make the trade contingent on Porter signing an extension. Graziano also reported that Dallas does not currently plan to extend him during the 2026 season.That puts Porter in a familiar position alongside former Steelers teammate George Pickens.Pittsburgh traded Pickens to Dallas before the 2025 season. He played without receiving the long-term deal he was seeking, then produced career highs in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns.Porter now gets a similar opportunity. He can play out the season, rebuild leverage and potentially test free agency in 2027 if Dallas does not use a franchise or transition tag.What does Joey Porter Jr. give a Cowboys secondary that badly needed help?Dallas did not make this move simply because Porter became available.The Cowboys entered Week 4 with one of the league’s most vulnerable secondaries. Cobie Durant was sidelined with a hamstring injury, while Shavon Revel Jr. was dealing with knee and ankle issues.The problems extend beyond availability.Through three games, opposing quarterbacks had completed 72.6% of their passes against Dallas, according to ESPN. The Cowboys also entered the week without an interception and had recorded only two sacks.Porter gives defensive coordinator Christian Parker a cornerback whose strengths match part of what Dallas already wants to do.ESPN reported that the Cowboys played man coverage on 24.8% of their defensive snaps through three games, slightly above the league average of 23.2%.Porter has built much of his reputation around man coverage. Since entering the NFL in 2023, opposing quarterbacks have completed 56% of their passes when he was the nearest defender, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That ranked 13th lowest among defenders with at least 100 targets over that span.Dallas clearly needed help. Owner and general manager Jerry Jones had already acknowledged that the Cowboys were discussing possible additions before the trade.“The answer to your question is yes, there's conversations going on,” Jones said during his Tuesday radio appearance.The Cowboys ultimately sent Pittsburgh a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round selection for Porter.His immediate availability remains uncertain. articles.title: From $490,000 to $100 million: How Tom Brady turned his NFL fame into a lasting charitable legacy
articles.summary: Tom Brady built one of the most decorated careers in NFL history, but his influence has extended far beyond football.
articles.body: Tom Brady built one of the most decorated careers in NFL history, but his influence has extended far beyond football. Long before his retirement, Brady became closely linked with Best Buddies, a nonprofit focused on creating opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. What began with his involvement as a volunteer grew into a two-decade partnership. By 2023, Best Buddies said Brady had helped the organisation raise more than $100 million, marking a remarkable chapter in his life away from the field.Tom Brady’s $490,000 start with Change the WorldBrady’s charitable story has an interesting starting point. In 2005, he established the Change the World Foundation and initially funded it with a $490,000 donation of his own money, according to reporting by The Washington Post based on Boston Globe research. The foundation later supported a range of causes and organisations connected to Brady’s interests.His relationship with Best Buddies had already become important by then. Brady first became involved with the organisation as a volunteer in 2003. Over the years, his role expanded well beyond simply lending his name to an event.Best Buddies says its mission centres on creating one-to-one friendships, employment opportunities, leadership development and inclusive living for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Brady became one of its most recognisable ambassadors, helping bring attention to that work through his enormous public profile.The relationship also developed into a significant fundraising partnership. In 2017, Best Buddies said that its 15-year partnership with Brady had helped it raise $46.5 million. The organisation also credited Brady with helping increase awareness of its mission and reach more supporters.That figure provides an important snapshot of how much the partnership had grown. Brady was not simply attending charity events. He was using the visibility that came with being an NFL superstar to bring supporters, sponsors and donors into the organisation's orbit.How Tom Brady helped Best Buddies reach $100 millionThe scale of Brady's involvement became even clearer several years later.In November 2023, Best Buddies honoured Brady with its Spirit of Leadership Award at its 25th Annual Best Buddies Gala in Miami. The organisation said Brady had served as a Global Ambassador for more than two decades and had helped raise more than $100 million for its work supporting people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.That $100 million figure needs some context. It does not mean Brady personally donated $100 million. Best Buddies attributes the fundraising total to his efforts and involvement with the organisation. His contribution included appearances, fundraising events, memorabilia, personal outreach and connections with sponsors and supporters.That distinction matters when looking at the financial side of Brady's philanthropy. His value to Best Buddies has largely come from his ability to attract attention and participation rather than simply writing enormous personal cheques.The organisation has described Brady as an advocate, friend and dedicated supporter. He has travelled for events, hosted gatherings and continued helping the charity connect with people in his wider network.His involvement also included fundraising challenges where fans and participants could directly contribute. In 2017, for example, Brady served as honorary co-chair of the Best Buddies Challenge: Hyannis Port. The event raised a record $6 million overall, while a football toss and auctions involving Brady raised $118,800 during the surrounding festivities. Team Tom Brady itself raised more than $721,000 that year.Those events show how his celebrity status became a fundraising tool. A football appearance could bring supporters through the door. A signed item could generate an auction bid. His presence could turn an ordinary charity gathering into a major event.Tom Brady’s personal foundation and the Best Buddies connectionBrady's charitable history also includes a complicated financial chapter involving Change the World Foundation.In 2017, The Washington Post reported on Boston Globe findings that Best Buddies had provided substantial funding to Brady's foundation. Through 2015, Best Buddies had supplied roughly $2.25 million of the foundation's $2.3 million in contributions after Brady's initial $490,000 donation. The reporting also noted that Best Buddies had pledged another $500,000 in 2017.The arrangement attracted scrutiny because money raised through Brady's work with Best Buddies also flowed toward his personal charitable interests. However, reporting at the time noted that independent charity watchdogs did not identify the arrangement as illegal. Sports Illustrated's legal analysis similarly explained that charities can legally support other charitable organisations while raising questions about the optics of this particular structure.Best Buddies defended the relationship by pointing to the results generated through Brady's involvement. Its founder and chairman, Anthony K. Shriver, said the partnership allowed the organisation to provide services to tens of thousands of people while keeping Brady involved with causes he cared about.The numbers provide some perspective. Best Buddies said in 2017 that its partnership with Brady had already generated $46.5 million for the organisation. By 2023, that figure had grown beyond $100 million.Why Tom Brady’s charitable legacy extends beyond footballBrady's NFL career gave him an extraordinary platform. Seven Super Bowl victories, multiple MVP awards and two decades at the centre of American football made his name instantly recognisable. But his work with Best Buddies shows another way an athlete can use that visibility.The organisation has continued to highlight the wider effects of Brady's involvement. Best Buddies says his support has helped with fundraising while also building awareness of initiatives involving friendship, employment, leadership development and inclusive housing.Brady has also spoken warmly about the people he met through the organisation. In a statement published by Best Buddies, he said:“It has been one of my greatest honors to serve as a Global Ambassador for Best Buddies,” said Tom Brady. “This organization has become a part of my life. I love meeting the inspiring buddies at events, seeing their smiles, and hearing them talk about how Best Buddies has changed their lives for the better by helping them make friends at school and find meaningful jobs in their local communities.”The statement captures an important part of his connection with the organisation. The relationship was not limited to fundraising totals. Brady repeatedly returned to events, met participants and remained involved over many years.In 2024, Best Buddies founder Anthony K. Shriver said Brady had chaired the organisation's Hyannis Port Challenge for 20 years and that the event alone had raised more than $100 million for Best Buddies programs.That makes the headline figure more meaningful. The journey from a $490,000 personal foundation contribution in 2005 to more than $100 million raised through his long-running Best Buddies involvement was not a single donation or one-night fundraiser. It developed over decades.For Tom Brady, the football legacy will always be defined by championships and records. His charitable work tells a different story, one built through appearances, relationships, fundraising and sustained involvement. articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Suddenly hot Browns with Deshaun Watson take on Steelers
articles.summary: The Browns and Steelers are both 2-1, coming off Week 3 wins.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns lost 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars in their opener. There was a question whether Deshaun Watson would get benched before Week 2. It seemed likely that if he got another start he'd still be replaced by Week 3, which was Cleveland's home opener.

The Browns have won two straight games. They had late rallies to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road and the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Watson hasn't been great, but he has been better than his first few disastrous seasons with the Browns, and there's no longer daily conversation over whether he'll get benched. This week the Browns go for a three-game winning streak Thursday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers , who are also off to a 2-1 start and tied for first place in the AFC North. All four teams in the division are 2-1.

The Steelers had a huge win Sunday, beating the Bengals 30-27. An offense that had scored only one touchdown through two games came alive. Aaron Rodgers had 292 yards passing, and Jaylen Warren had 127 yards rushing. Warren will be in for another big workload this week with Rico Dowdle ruled out due to a toe injury.

For the Browns, the offensive resurgence has been incremental. Watson had 238 and 144 yards in Cleveland's last two games, but that has been enough to help the team to wins. There is a good young core around the quarterback that is emerging and contributing each of the past two weeks. After the first game of the season it seemed impossible that the Browns might spend any days alone in first place of the division, but that's where they'll be with a win Thursday night.

The rivalry between the Browns and Steelers goes back decades and runs deep. This time there are some considerable early-season stakes.

It's a dead heat. Both teams are 2-1. Both have questions about their long-term viability as contenders in the AFC North because of their uneven offenses. Perhaps the Browns get the edge because it's a home game and if they lose, it will be tough to find road wins in the division to even it out. But these two teams should be pleased to be 2-1, and one of them is going to be 3-1 (let's assume there won't be a tie) and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North for a few days.

The Browns are 2-1, and one would assume that means they've run the ball well. Actually, Cleveland has been one of the worst teams in the NFL on the ground. The Browns are 29th in rushing yards, 29th in rushing yards per attempt and have zero rushing touchdowns. They're 31st in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush. Judkins, in his second season, has just 124 yards and is averaging 3 yards per attempt. Last season he was averaging 3.6 per attempt before dislocating his ankle and fracturing his fibula.

Perhaps that leg injury is lingering. With Deshaun Watson not producing many yards in the air, the Browns need the running game to emerge to have a consistent offense. Judkins is the key to that. He has 42 rushing attempts this season and no other running back has more than four. Judkins has to start producing for the Browns' offense to stay afloat.

We probably won't be telling our grandkids about this game, but it remains an important game in the AFC North. The Steelers opened as 2.5-point road favorites, and the line has moved to Pittsburgh -3 at several sportsbooks. The total is a low one at 38.5, up slightly from the opener. This will be the eighth straight game that Cleveland has been an underdog and the 12th time in its last 13 games, dating back to last season. Aaron Rodgers and Pittsburgh's offense looked downright functional in Week 3 against Cincinnati , while Deshaun Watson did enough to lead the Browns past Carolina late on Sunday. Cleveland's defense (17th in EPA/play) hasn't been as strong as it has been in previous seasons. I'd look to the over in this game, even as ugly as it feels to take.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

Expectations have to be somewhat muted as the Steelers and Browns kick off Week 4, as the 38.5 total is the lowest of the week. Here are three fantasy themes to consider as you watch the game.

1. Is Harold Fannin Jr. the first read in Cleveland's passing game? Fannin had a quiet opener, but he's posted a 12-105-2 line since, taking advantage of 15 targets. He overcame the messy QB play in Cleveland last year, and Deshaun Watson's play the last two weeks has been encouraging.

2. Will the Jaylen Warren show continue? Warren finished as the RB8 last week, given the backfield to himself with Rico Dowdle unavailable. Dowdle won't play here, which means Warren can push for 20 or more touches against a Cleveland run defense that's been ordinary (4.5 YPC allowed).

3. Can Quinshon Judkins find room to run? Judkins has seen a touch increase every week, but he's still struggling to find space to operate (3.0 YPC). Cleveland's offensive line is one of the worst in football, but at least it's up against a Pittsburgh front seven that's been merely average.

articles.title: Week 4 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice on Fantasy Football Stars to Play or Bench
articles.summary: Week 4 will get underway on Thursday night with a battle between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns that will, at least temporarily, determine first place in the AFC North.
articles.body:
Week 4 will get underway on Thursday night with a battle between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns that will, at least temporarily, determine first place in the AFC North.

Similarly, fantasy managers will be looking to stay ahead of the proverbial pack as the season approaches the quarter mark. Lineup decisions will be critical, and while some starts are obvious, others may require a deeper dive.

Who can managers trust in Week 4? Let's dive into the most recent results and the looming matchups for some start/sit recommendations.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is still looking to recapture his 2024 form. He's thrown just three touchdown passes through three games and hasn't regularly tested his surgically repaired Achilles as a scrambler.

articles.title: New Zach Charbonnet Injury Update, Return Timeline After Seahawks Open RB's Practice Window
articles.summary: A slow start this season for the Seattle Seahawks' rushing attack could get a boost soon with Zach Charbonnet taking a significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL suffered in the playoffs last season.
articles.body:
A slow start this season for the Seattle Seahawks' rushing attack could get a boost soon with Zach Charbonnet taking a significant step in his recovery from a torn ACL suffered in the playoffs last season.

The Seahawks announced on Thursday they have opened Charbonnet's practice window, making him eligible to practice this week and potentially return as soon as Week 5.

Charbonnet tore his ACL in the second quarter of Seattle's 41-6 victory over the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC Divisional Round. The game was played on Jan. 17, all but ensuring he wouldn't be ready to go at the start of the season.

Seattle made that official by keeping Charbonnet on the physically unable to perform list after final roster cuts were due on Aug. 30.

Seahawks general manager John Schneider told reporters at the time there was never any serious consideration to taking Charbonnet off the PUP list at the end of the preseason.

Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Wednesday that Charbonnet's return to game action is a "matter of how many practices they need, roster spots and things like that."

League rules require a player activated off the PUP list to be added to the 53-man roster after 21 days or miss the remainder of the season. The 21-day window means Charbonnet has to be added to the active roster by Oct. 22.

The first game Charbonnet will be eligible to play is against the 49ers on Oct. 11.

Kenneth Walker III, who was named Super Bowl 60 MVP, left the Seahawks in free agency to sign with the Kansas City Chiefs.

Seattle has split running back duties so far this season between Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson.

Price has started each game thus far, but he has yet to play more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in any contest. The Notre Dame alum has also lost a fumble in each of the past two weeks.

Wilson leads the Seahawks with 32 carries, 21 of which came in Week 2 against the Arizona Cardinals. George Holani had a season-high eight carries in Week 3.

Charbonnet had his most productive season in 2025 with career-highs in rushing attempts (184), rushing yards (730) and rushing touchdowns (12).

articles.title: Drake Maye's Shoulder Got 'Dinged,' Patriots' McDaniels Says amid Injury Concerns
articles.summary: After Drake Maye's surprise appearance on the injury report this week, New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels spoke about the shoulder issue for his star quarterback.
articles.body:
After Drake Maye's surprise appearance on the injury report this week, New England Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels spoke about the shoulder issue for his star quarterback.

McDaniels told reporters on Thursday that Maye's shoulder got "dinged" in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3.

Maye was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice and doesn't appear to be in any danger of missing this week's game against the Buffalo Bills.

An ugly start to the season in which Maye has thrown six interceptions to one touchdown has led to discussion this week about the relationship between the Patriots quarterback and head coach Mike Vrabel.

After WEEI's Greg Hill said on the radio earlier this week there are rumblings of an "issue" between the two, both Maye and Vrabel have downplayed things.

Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday that Maye was the reason he originally took the Patriots' head-coaching job in January 2025.

Maye said after Wednesday's practice that Vrabel is "one of the best football coaches I've had in my life" and he loves playing for him.

During the same press conference, Maye also downplayed that his shoulder is going to be a hindrance of any kind.

"I wouldn't say there is a problem with my shoulder," Maye said. "You're going to get banged up every now and then, but at the same time, a lot of guys are banged up."

Maye has been at the center of the offensive issues in New England so far this season. The offense has committed eight turnovers through three games, with him responsible for seven of them (six interceptions, one lost fumble).

During his MVP runner-up campaign in 2025, Maye had a total of 11 turnovers in 17 regular-season games. He has been sacked three times in each of the first three games this season.

Some of the issues can be attributed to a receiver room that desperately needs A.J. Brown back healthy. Mack Hollins currently leads the team with 12 receptions and 156 receiving yards.

A victory over the undefeated Bills would definitely do a lot to calm the fears bubbling up in New England right now. It would also put the Patriots right back in the mix in the AFC East.

The Patriots (1-2) and Bills (3-0) will kickoff from Highmark Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Has 'Impressed' Giants in Practice After Vikings Trade, Matt Nagy Says
articles.summary: New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy likes what he has seen so far from recently acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy.
articles.body:
New York Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy likes what he has seen so far from recently acquired quarterback J.J. McCarthy.

Speaking to reporters Thursday, Nagy said of McCarthy, "He's done a great job with it. We're impressed, it's impressive. But at the same point in time, we also understand that it can be a lot, so it's a little bit of a balance."

Nagy noted that he didn't "know a whole lot" about McCarthy before his arrival, but he has gotten "good reviews" from those he has talked to, and he has admired the "grind" McCarthy has shown this week.

With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart ruled out for the remainder of the regular season due to a knee injury, the Giants sent a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy on Monday.

McCarthy was selected 10th overall by the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft, but he never developed into the franchise quarterback the franchise hoped it was getting.

After missing his entire rookie season with a knee injury, McCarthy started 10 games last season. He posted a winning record at 6-4, but completed only 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, while also rushing for 181 yards and four touchdowns.

McCarthy lost the QB1 competition with Kyler Murray during training camp and the preseason, and he also fell behind Carson Wentz on the depth chart, making him Minnesota's third quarterback.

The writing was on the wall regarding McCarthy's future with the Vikings at that point, and it seemed it was only a matter of time before the Vikes moved on.

With Dart's injury leaving veteran Jameis Winston as the only established quarterback on New York's roster, the Giants made the move to acquire McCarthy.

While McCarthy is starting off as the backup to Winston, a starting opportunity could present itself at some point during the 2026 season if Winston gets injured or struggles.

McCarthy is likely to suit up for the Giants for the first time on Sunday when New York hosts the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: Falcons' Bijan Robinson Drops Kobe Bryant Quote While Reflecting on Huge Primetime Performances
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are a primetime staple in the early going of the 2026 campaign, which is bad news for opposing defenses that have to face Bijan Robinson.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are a primetime staple in the early going of the 2026 campaign, which is bad news for opposing defenses that have to face Bijan Robinson.

"I love what Kobe said," Robinson said of playing in primetime, per Josh Kendall of The Athletic. "They pay to watch you, so you have to do your job."

As Kendall noted, the star running back has averaged 185.8 yards from scrimmage in his last six primetime contests dating back to the 2025 campaign.

His latest unbelievable performance under the national spotlight came on Thursday Night Football in Week 3 when he torched the Green Bay Packers in a 35-14 victory. Robinson ended up with 194 rushing yards, 19 receiving yards and two touchdowns as a blur on the field who left Packers defenders grasping at air a number of times.

It may have been a sign of things to come as well considering Atlanta's next two games against the New Orleans Saints and Baltimore Ravens are also primetime contests.

The Falcons are just 1-2 on the season, but the win over Green Bay was the first time starting quarterback Michael Penix was under center after Cooper Rush and Jack Strand were under center before he was cleared.

The Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers were able to stack the box to account for Robinson without having to worry about being beaten over the top, but Penix showed an immediate connection with Drake London.

London finished with nine catches for 194 yards against the Packers, highlighting how opposing defenses have to pick their poison with the wide receiver and Robinson in the same offense.

If Robinson's comments are any indication, it could be more of the same in primetime against the Saints.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels does not dismiss playing Sunday against the Colts in London after ugly elbow dislocation injury
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels spoke to reporters in London and hinted he could return Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts after his elbow dislocation injury.
articles.body: Jayden Daniels' journey through his elbow dislocation 11 days ago has been a rollercoaster ride, especially if you saw how the injury happened, and the concern that it ended his season prematurely. But we've reached the point where the Washington Commanders quarterback is talking to the media again and even suggesting he might play on Sunday. Daniels, in London with his teammates for the game against the Indianapolis Colts, faced reporters for the first time since his injury on Sept. 20 and was almost immediately asked if he could play this week. "It feels good," Daniels said of his left elbow, which was also dislocated last season. "Feels good to be back and, you know, taking it day by day." WASHINGTON COMMANDERS FACE SEASON-DEFINING CRISIS AS JAYDEN DANIELS SUFFERS ANOTHER SERIOUS ELBOW INJURY Daniels has practiced the past two days to varying degrees. Is he surprised that he's been able to get back on the field this soon? "What you think?" Daniels playfully responded to the question. "I'm not surprised. No, everything I went through, you know, everybody said, I'd be good to go if I'm able to go out there on Sunday, but again, just taking it day by day." So, um, the money question: Is he indeed playing on Sunday? Daniels smiled. " Just taking the day by day," he replied. COMMANDERS PLAYERS PUSH BACK ON THE NARRATIVE THEY DIDN'T CARE ABOUT JAYDEN DANIELS INJURY Looking for a no, in that response. Not there. In fact, a source close to Daniels told OutKick that while he is "not pushing coaches" to play on Sunday, that is exactly what he wants to do. But it's not ultimately his decision. Coach Dan Quinn on Wednesday said the team wants to gauge how Daniels looks in practices this week before making a final decision on whether to start backup Marcus Mariota or return Daniels to the lineup. "As we're working through the week, he'll get more [repetitions in practice]," Quinn said. "It's part of our return-to-play process where guys do individual, that kind of limited portion, then some of the team reps and then more. "As we get into Thursday and Friday, we'll see what that load looks like. And by Friday, we'll have a definite determination of where we're at." Looking for the part where Quinn says Daniels is out. Not there. It does not take Sherlock Holmes to figure out that while in London, the Commanders are sounding almost hopeful about their starting quarterback's status. And part of that is leaving the door ajar for his return this week. This is a bit surprising because in the days after the elbow injury, there was a real possibility Daniels could require surgery and be out the remainder of the season. Then Daniels met with multiple medical experts and decided wearing a brace, while affecting the functionality to his non-throwing arm, would be acceptable. His return to play is not a pain tolerance issue. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! So, Daniels decided to return – be that this week or the next, barring a setback. "I love football. I play football," Daniels said in explaining his reason for returning. "I mean, I get paid to play football, so, I went to my teammates and stuff like that to see that everybody's hurting. Something's wrong with everybody on this team. "So, I just feel like just for me, just being a leader, being a guy, just going out there and, give it my shot to go out there and play and obviously protect myself, you know, stuff like that. "But, you know, I just love football. I have a passion for it." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.body: Welcome to the latest edition of True Romance. For whatever reason, this week we're being hit from all sorts of angles with tales of cheating. In fact, she revealed during a recent episode of her Booked, Blonde & Busy podcast that she had been cheated on in all of her past relationships. But she finally realized after the third time it happened that she wasn't the problem. Forget that common denominator nonsense. Ponton has it figured out. "I think cheating is a sign of insecurity," she said. "If you feel the need to be in a happy, healthy relationship with somebody, and go to get outside validation that you are attractive, that is not a reflection of this perfectly great person that could be in your life. That is a reflection on them. That’s my hot take." She's the perfectly great person that you're now missing out on. Well, not the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback. He presumably isn't seeking outside validation that he's attractive. Good for him. INNOCENT WRESTLING WITH SISTER OF WIFE'S BEST FRIEND REVEALS CHEATING WITH A TWIST, MCDONALD'S WEDDING & SIGNS Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook and keep sending your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer). If you can believe it, Brooke Hogan says her dad sleeping with her friend changed their relationship I think you're just going to have to trust me on this one. Call me crazy, but I believe Brooke Hogan when she says her relationship with Hulk Hogan changed after she says he slept with her friend. She's a forgiving person, so that wasn’t the issue. She forgave her dad, but the relationship they had prior to him sleeping with one of her best friends was gone. How you ask? It's one of life's mysteries. "A major turning point came after he slept with my friend Christiane [Plante]," Brooke told Us Magazine. "I forgive people very easily — sometimes probably too easily — and I forgave him, but something between us changed afterward. I don’t think he ever related to me in quite the same way again." The Hulkster was known to run wild on occasion. This relationship with her friend might have been one of those times. But all wasn’t lost. Hooking up with her friend, her parent's divorce, and everything that went along with it, didn’t mean she didn’t still care for Hulk. "I can love my father profoundly and still tell the truth about where he hurt me," Brooke added. "I can acknowledge the wonderful things my family gave me while also acknowledging that eventually the dynamic became something I could no longer live inside. Both things can be true." Exactly. It's all about forgiveness. I think this is a lesson that a lot of us can learn from, including another of the stories we're going to get into. Woman's sister hooked up with a guy she went on a date with How long is too long to hold a grudge with your sister just because she slept with a guy that you went on a date with? A week? A month? A year? How about six years? This wasn’t a guy that she was in a serious relationship with. This was a guy she really liked is all. Yet she still hasn't gotten over it. "My sister and I lived together and I went on a date with a guy I really liked. I introduced them before he and I went out and I thought we had a great time. She wasn't home when I got back but we texted a little and I told her I had the best time, etc. She told me not to wait up for her so I didn't," she wrote on Reddit. "The next morning I was making breakfast when I heard her coming in and I saw my date from the day before with her. He ran away once he saw me but she couldn't hide what they did. She was giggling and it was clear she had been with someone. I made breakfast and then hid in my room from her for the rest of the day and texted my brothers." She's off to a decent start. She sees her sister coming in after a night out and her date is there. She knows by the look on her sister's face that they slept together and instead of a confrontation right there, she stuffs her feelings deep inside and hides out in her room. "When I was still avoiding her the next day she barged into my room and asked me what was wrong and why I was avoiding her and I broke down and told her she hurt me when she slept with my date. Her whole demeanor changed and it was like she had no idea that might have hurt my feelings," she continued. "She apologized but I didn't want to hear it and I told her to leave me alone. She asked me what she could do and she promised she'd never sleep with him again and she'd tell him to take me out again but that made it worse. I stayed a few more days but moved in with my brother when I realized I couldn't keep living with her and I didn't forgive her just because she said she was sorry." Since then, she's been "civil" with her sister, but they’re not hanging out or doing anything together. Those days are gone. Things came to a head recently when one of their brothers told the sister's boyfriend, who she was in a serious relationship with, about the incident. The sister thinks it's time to get over it. "She was upset with our brother but then she told me I needed to get over what she did because it was one stupid decision and she is too damn good of a sister to let one thing ruin us," she added. "She also defended what she did because she doesn't think what she did was bad, which honestly was what I suspected all along." The reason she suspected it all along is because that's the truth. This wasn’t a guy she was planning to marry. It was one date, and sure the timing wasn't great, but better to find out what this guy is all about immediately. She should be thanking her sister, not dragging this out for this long. Couples who have been together 10–20+ years: what brought the spark back? This one proves there's not a single way that couples who have put time in together keep the spark going or bring it back. You really have to find what works for you. I think that's the lesson here. articles.title: Jayden Daniels returns to Commanders' practice, not concerned about potentially reinjuring elbow
articles.summary: Daniels dislocated his left elbow in Week 2 and will wear a brace for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was a limited participant for a second straight practice as he begins working his way toward a return to the field after dislocating his left elbow in Week 2 .

Daniels will sport a brace on his left arm for the rest of the season that will see his elbow bent slightly in order to avoid another dislocation. The third-year signal-caller said he is not concerned about reinjury once he's back on the field.

"That's what the brace is for," Daniels said Thursday , three days before the Commanders meet the Indianapolis Colts in London. "If I had that concern, I would have gotten surgery."

After meeting with several specialists , Daniels was not recommended to have surgery . But a procedure could be on the table come the offseason.

"Obviously you have those conversations with people I need to have those conversations with," Daniels said via ESPN . "If the surgery was needed to be ASAP, then I've got to do what's best for me. We had those conversations. I was blessed enough to go back out there on the practice field. ... I'm not really concerned at this moment."

Daniels suffered the injury in his non-throwing arm during the team's loss to the Dallas Cowboys . It is the same elbow he dislocated and reinjured last season. After sitting out last week, he joined the team on the flight to England this week. Head coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday there is still "a chance" the quarterback could play, but "we're not going to put him out there before he's ready."

For now, Daniels is "taking it day by day" and it's not yet known if he will be available to play in Week 4. Marcus Mariota would get a second straight start if Daniels ends up being ruled out.

"I love playing football, I get paid to play football," Daniels said. "Everybody is hurting. I just feel for me being a leader, go out there and give it my shot to go out and play and obviously protect myself. I just love football and have a passion for it."

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Used 75 Different Hand Signals at Line of Scrimmage in 2025, Steelers' Howard Says
articles.summary: Upon his arrival to the Pittsburgh Steelers before the 2025 season, veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers had an interesting priority.
articles.body:
Upon his arrival to the Pittsburgh Steelers before the 2025 season, veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers had an interesting priority.

Steelers backup quarterback Will Howard told Jori Epstein of Yahoo Sports that on the first day of last season's training camp, Rodgers had him create a Google Doc with his hand signals.

"He gave me kind of the baseline of like, 'All right, hitch, slant, routes, a couple of combinations here and there, some formation signals …'" Howard said. "We would kind of evolve it as we went. So it started off with probably 25, 30 signals and then it ended up being like 75 by the end of [the season]."

Epstein noted that she received coach and player estimates on hand signals from other teams, and Rodgers' 75 far exceeds the Denver Broncos' 15-25, Baltimore Ravens' 20-30, and Philadelphia Eagles and Seattle Seahawks' 50-60.

Rodgers has always been known for his detailed approach to the game, but even the most meticulous players can have trouble remembering all 75 gestures.

"It's a lot of signals," Steelers receiver DK Metcalf told Epstein. "But I mean, they help us win football games at the end of the day when we're all connected."

Still, at 42 years old, it's safe to say that Rodgers won't be changing his approach in what is likely his final NFL season.

"He definitely takes pride in the signals," Steelers receiver Ben Skowronek said. "And then sometimes he signals something [in practice] that maybe he used in the past and you're like, 'What the f--k is that, Aaron?'"

Rodgers and the Steelers will try to improve to 3-1 when they face the Cleveland Browns (2-1) on Thursday Night Football .

articles.title: Ben Johnson Reveals the One Upside to Caleb Williams’ Injury
articles.summary: Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury remains a problem the Chicago Bears want solved as quickly and carefully as possible. No one […]
articles.body:
Caleb Williams ' hamstring injury remains a problem the Chicago Bears want solved as quickly and carefully as possible. No one inside Halas Hall is pretending otherwise.

Williams is the face of the franchise, the quarterback Ben Johnson was hired to develop and the player the Bears expect to lead them through the biggest games of the season. His Grade 2 hamstring strain has already kept him out of one game, and Chicago is still not publicly committing to a precise return date.

But Johnson sees one potential benefit in Williams' stint on the sideline. The Bears coach believes the young quarterback can learn by watching how a 15-year NFL veteran prepared for the opportunity.

Case Keenum took over as Chicago's starter against the Eagles after Williams was sidelined and Tyson Bagent 's concussion disrupted his practice week. The 38-year-old had not started a regular-season game since 2023, yet he calmly led the Bears to a 27-7 win over Philadelphia .

Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns. He added a rushing touchdown, avoided turnovers and did not take a sack. More than the statistics, though, Johnson was impressed by the way Keenum prepared for the moment.

"There's a tremendous amount to be gained," Johnson said of Williams watching the process from the outside. The coach pointed to the value of seeing the full preparation picture and watching a different quarterback take control of the offense for a week.

Williams has spent most of his NFL career learning through repetition. He takes the snaps, directs the huddle, works through mistakes on the practice field and then has to execute in a game. That is the most valuable form of development for any young quarterback.

But watching from the sideline can create a different kind of learning opportunity.

A quarterback who is not consumed by calling the next play can study how the entire offense functions. He can observe the communication between coaches and players, notice what makes the game plan work and watch a veteran anticipate the answers to a defense before the ball is snapped.

Keenum gave Williams an example of that preparation last week. Johnson described the Bears' pregame quarterback meeting as a major part of the routine. With Keenum preparing to start, the meeting had a different feel. The veteran's experience showed in how he reviewed the plan, understood the concepts and approached the details of the matchup.

Keenum has spent more than a decade playing for different coaching staffs, learning different systems and preparing for every kind of role. He has been a starter, a backup, a mentor and an emergency option. That career path gave him a body of knowledge that a young quarterback simply does not yet have.

Johnson believes Williams can take something from it.

The Bears don't need Williams to become Keenum. Williams' talent is different. His mobility, arm strength and ability to create outside structure are part of what makes him special. Chicago's offense will always be better when Williams is healthy and able to use those gifts, but Keenum's performance against Philadelphia offered a reminder that quarterback play is not only about talent.

Keenum got the ball out quickly against an Eagles front that can wreck games. He recognized pressure, relied on his pass catchers to be where they were supposed to be and avoided putting the offense in bad situations. The Bears did not ask him to play like Williams. They asked him to operate the offense with clarity and confidence.

He did exactly that. For Williams, the lesson is not that he should stop using his athleticism or become a checkdown quarterback. It is that the explosive plays can become even more dangerous when the routine plays are handled decisively.

The Bears have spent the season emphasizing the importance of staying on schedule. Drew Brees delivered a similar message to Williams before the opener, stressing the value of easy completions, checkdowns and smart throwaways. Williams responded with an efficient Week 1 performance against Carolina before the injury interrupted his momentum.

Keenum's week was not glamorous. It was long meetings, exhaustive film work and a level of preparation that allowed him to step into a difficult assignment without appearing overwhelmed. Johnson said Williams can benefit from hearing how a veteran like Keenum works through that process.

That does not make the hamstring injury a blessing. It could cost Williams multiple games, and Chicago will be cautious because a rushed return would risk a setback. The Bears need their franchise quarterback healthy for the stretch run, not merely available for one early-October game.

Still, the injury does not have to mean a lost developmental week. Williams can remain engaged in meetings, help analyze the game plan and absorb how another quarterback handles leadership duties. When he returns, the Bears hope he will have gained a wider perspective on the offense he is still learning to master.

Keenum's job was to keep Chicago afloat.

In the process, he may have helped teach Williams something that lasts much longer.

articles.title: NFL opens Pandora's box by supposedly admitting DPI error to Sean McVay
articles.summary: It's unclear whether McVay was authorized to disclose his communications with the league.
articles.body:
If gambling is permitted freely on sporting events, normal incidents of the game such as bad snaps, dropped passes, turnovers, penalties, and play calling inevitably will fuel speculation, distrust, and accusations of point-shaving or game-fixing.

Commissioner Roger Goodell uttered those words, back when the NFL hated gambling. With the league now getting rich(er) from its association with sportsbooks, it needs to be thinking about how those "normal incidents of the game" can create problems, if they're not handled properly.

Transparency, obviously, is critical. For a level of the sport that prides itself on setting the agenda, it has fallen woefully behind the UFL and multiple college conferences when it comes to peeling back the officiating curtain and letting the fans understand why certain calls are made.

A separate potential exists for unforced errors. The NFL has made one, in two different respects.

First, assuming that someone from the league did indeed tell Rams coach Sean McVay that defensive pass interference shouldn't have been called on L.A. cornerback Josh Wallace with the game on the line, why would the league do this? Beyond the fact that the league has thrown the official who made the call under the bus, this wasn't an objective mistake.

Pass interference is a judgment call. It's discretionary. And the DPI foul appeared to fall within that band of discretion — especially since it seemed to us to be the right call, given that Wallace used his forearm to shove Broncos receiver Pat Bryant as the pass was arriving.

Second, was McVay authorized to tell the world that the league had acknowledged an error (if the league truly did)? Those communications are confidential. Last year, when Ravens coach John Harbaugh disclosed that the league acknowledged an objective blunder on an unnecessary roughness call arising from a hit on Pittsburgh 's long snapper, Harbaugh expressly said he had permission from the league to share that information .

McVay didn't say that. It's possible he ran afoul of the league's expectation that such discussions won't be disclosed.

Given the clear connection between the call and the outcome, the NFL shouldn't want a head coach to state that the league office admitted to a mistake. What's next? A refund of all moneyline bets on the Rams?

It's one thing for a normal incident of the game to fuel the tinfoil-hat crowd. It's quite another for an abnormal decision to be made to admit that a plausibly accurate subjective decision was wrong. Beyond fueling conspiracy theories, it could spark a long line of losing bettors who will demand a refund.

articles.title: Did Mike Tomlin’s Minecraft obsession derail NFL coaching career?
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin may have spent too much time building his Minecraft city.
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin spent 12 years building an enormous Minecraft city while coaching the Pittsburgh Steelers . So, naturally, NFL fans now have questions.

Tomlin revealed his secret hobby months after leaving Pittsburgh in early 2026. He started playing Minecraft on PlayStation 3 to connect with his children. The kids eventually moved on. Tomlin did not.

He kept transferring the same world across console generations. That journey eventually reached the PlayStation 5, where Tomlin continued expanding his virtual city.

That raises one extremely important football question: Did Minecraft cost Tomlin a few playoff wins?

Tomlin coached Pittsburgh from 2007 through 2025. During his first seven seasons, the Steelers reached two Super Bowls and won one Lombardi Trophy. Additionally, in that span, the Steelers' playoff record stood at 5-3.

Over his final 12 seasons, Pittsburgh failed to reach another Super Bowl. The Steelers also went 3-9 in the playoffs during that span, which coincidentally aligns with Tomlin's time playing Minecraft.

NFL star T.J. Ward speaks about Mike Tomlin's Minecraft hobby

Denver , Colorado, USA; NBC broadcast analyst Mike Tomlin at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Former NFL star T.J. Ward also noticed the timing.

"My first thought was definitely, when did he start playing and when was the last playoff game won?" Ward said on Speakeasy . "Is that why they ain't win a playoff game?"

Ward then admitted that Minecraft is harder than it looks, saying, "That [expletive] is hard."

Later, Ward could not resist taking another shot. He said, "I think he spent a lot of valuable time creating that city. Some time where I think he could have been using preparing for a football game."

Of course, there is no evidence Tomlin skipped film sessions to build skyscrapers. NFL coaching is complicated, and playoff results involve far more than one hobby.

Tomlin now has more time for his virtual city after stepping down from Pittsburgh in January. Perhaps retirement finally gives him enough hours to finish downtown.

And if the next Minecraft update suddenly includes a Lombardi Trophy, we may have our answer.

articles.summary: Who knows how the Dallas Cowboys pried Joey Porter Jr. away from the Steelers. But the deal made blockbuster NFL waves. Furthermore, the Cowboys’ defensive...
articles.body:
Who knows how the Dallas Cowboys pried Joey Porter Jr. away from the Steelers . But the deal made blockbuster NFL waves . Furthermore, the Cowboys ' defensive coordinator shared his completely honest thoughts on adding Porter to his side of the ball, according to a post on X by Jon Machota.

"Cowboys DC Christian Parker on CB Joey Porter Jr. : 'He certainly fits what we do and how we want to play. When you have opportunities, and I get asked about guys like that, it's usually a yes. I'm always trying to add more good players.' "

Porter is a fourth-year NFL player. He finished fifth in the AP defensive rookie of the year voting in 2023. In that season, he started 11 games and defended 10 passes with an interception and 43 tackles. Last year with the Steelers , Porter totaled 14 passes defended with an interception and 52 tackles.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Did the Cowboys get a major upgrade with CB Joey Porter Jr.?

The Cowboys seem desperate to fix their defense. But one thing in this trade could work against them. Players who sit out through training camp and miss early games tend to be candidates for soft-tissue injuries that can linger throughout the season.

Whether Porter escapes that possibility remains to be seen. But he should beef up a thin Cowboys secondary, according to Bleacher Report.

"When Joey Porter Jr. is ready to take the field, he'll be the Cowboys' clear-cut No. 1 cover man on the boundary," Moe Moton wrote. "Through three seasons in Pittsburgh , he recorded 31 pass breakups, three interceptions, and allowed a 57.2 passer rating in coverage. Touted for his man coverage ability out of Penn State, he can shadow lead wide receivers and force quarterbacks to target secondary pass-catchers. Dallas should be far better in pass coverage going forward, as long as Porter's back injury clears up."

And the Cowboys didn't have to give up a premier pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. Jerry Jones is wheeling and dealing like a madman. He struck gold with George Pickens . Can he fleece the Steelers a second time?

articles.title: NFL predictions: BBV staff weighs in on Giants-Cardinals matchup
articles.summary: Can the New York Giants make the first quarter of their 2026 season a truly good one by defeating the Arizona Cardinals to improve their record to 3-1? Here...
articles.body:
Can the New York Giants make the first quarter of their 2026 season a truly good one by defeating the Arizona Cardinals to improve their record to 3-1? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the NFL Week 4 slate.

I think this game is going to be extremely telling as to who the 2026 Giants are. This will be offense's first game with Jameis Winston going through a normal week of practice and preparation.

That'll eliminate the excuses we've heard regarding the game plan against the Rams, as well as the short week and elements last week. Will the Giants trust Winston to throw the ball? And how will he execute if they do? Excuses aside, Winston hasn't looked good since Dart went down. The Giants will need him to step up if Arizona focuses on shutting down the Giants' run game.

On the defensive side of the ball, we'll get to see how the Giants adapt to losing their best player in Brian Burns . The Cardinals put up points against the 49ers, but was that just divisional weirdness? They only scored once against the Seahawks the week before.

I'm going to pick the Giants here, and I'm doing so because of one thing that stood out from Sunday: Multiple veterans of the 2025 Giants all saying some variation of "We don't win this game last year."

Sometimes winning isn't pretty. Sometimes it really is just surviving and making one fewer mistake than the other guy. And understanding that they can claw their way through adversity and not collapse could be bigger than we realize for this team. I still think the Giants still have the pieces in place to be the same team we saw against Dallas — assuming Jameis Winston can step up. It might not be pretty, and special teams may be the difference in the game, but I think the Giants do enough to win and keep moving forward.

To me these are two evenly matched teams. I wouldn't have said that after Game 1, but the Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns injuries lower the Giants' level of play on both sides of the ball. The forecast for Sunday is cloudy with a chance of showers. Assuming we don't get anything like the rain and winds of last weekend, my guess would be a high-scoring game. The Cards' defensive line is about as good as Tennessee 's, with Zaven Collins playing great outside and Roy Lopez solid in the middle, but like the Giants, they don't get much pass rush overall and can be run on. The secondary is nothing special either; their best-known player, Budda Baker , is not what he used to be.

The bigger problem is the Cards' offense. Jacoby Brissett is a seen by many as a quality backup-caliber QB, but he has been the starter at least part of the time for five different seasons. Last year he passed for over 3,000 yards and 23 TDs. His favorite target is All-Pro tight end Trey McBride , who has had 1,000 receiving yards two years in a row, and we know the Giants never shut down good tight ends. Brissett can also go to WR Michael Wilson , who also broke 1,000 yards last season. With Brian Burns out, unless Dennard Wilson finds a way to get his rushers to the QB, the Cards can put up a lot of points – they've broken 30 twice, against the good defenses of the Chargers and 49ers. Rookie RB Jeremiah Love had his best game so far last week with 90 yards, more than half after contact.

That said, the Giants can move the ball and put points up themselves if we get good Jameis rather than bad Jameis this week and if the rain holds off. Cam Skattebo should find room to run and the Giants' receivers should get open enough for them to sustain drives. I can even imagine this being a breakout week for Malik Nabers in which he starts to resemble the force of nature that he was in his rookie year.

Overall, I see the Cards having more firepower and coming out on top, say 31-27 if the rain is not a factor.

We are about to learn A LOT about this 2-1 Giants' team. The Cardinals have been respectable through two weeks and sit at 1-2. They've run an efficient quick game, earning them the seventh-highest EPA while running the fifth-most short passes. Brissett has been pressured the sixth most in the league, but the Giants generate the LEAST amount of pressure in the league. Arizona is going to throw quickly to mitigate Abdul Carter and the Giants' pass rush, which is now significantly worse without Brian Burns. We'll see new looks from Dennard Wilson's defense with the addition of Jihad Ward , but the Giants' cornerbacks MUST make plays on the football, and the defense, overall, must rally and tackle to prevent yards after the catch.

The Giants' offense has struggled to create explosive plays, and the Cardinals' defense has struggled to stop them. Arizona's defense hasn't blitz much ( 27th in blitz rate ), nor do they get much pressure ( 25th in pressure rate ), but Jameis Winston has a tendency to hold onto the football. The Giants are going to use heavier personnel, putting Arizona in a spot to use their BASE defense, which currently ranks 27th in EPA. I expect the Giants to lean on their rushing attack and attempt to run out of 11 personnel, where Arizona will match with nickel ( 27th in EPA in nickel defense ).

The Giants will work the play-action and attempt to get Malik Nabers going when they do throw the football, but expect a conservative approach, again, and one that embodies what we've discussed since John Harbaugh took the job — physical, heavy personnel, control the clock, and don't turn the football over. Winston must be cautious with the football. Again, I can see this going in many different ways, but I'll project a low-scoring victory for the Giants, but we'll see improvement in the red zone, and the Giants score two touchdowns.

Before the season started, Arizona at home in Week 4 looked like one of the safer "wins" on the schedule for Big Blue. Well, guess what? The Cardinals are favored by 2 1/2 points on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. That's how fast things can change in the NFL.

The Giants narrowly escaped with a win over the Titans in the wind and rain last week, and this week's injury loss for the season is another very costly one: Edge Brian Burns. New York must again regroup in the face of adversity.

The 1-2 Cardinals were supposed to be among the very worst teams in the league this season, but so far, they've been pretty frisky, and competitive despite a really tough schedule to open the season (@LAC, SEA, @SF). They've got weapons on offense that could give the depleted Giants' defense some real problems – Trey McBride is an elite talent at tight end, rookie RB Jeremiyah Love is dangerously explosive and saw his role expand last week, and WR Michael Wilson came out of nowhere last season and is a very capable receiver. Jacoby Brissett isn't afraid to chuck the ball all over the field.

I really want to take the Giants to win and get to 3-1 on Sunday, but I'm having trouble convincing myself that it's the smart pick. I'm willing to chalk up a lot of the offensive malaise in Jameis Winston's first two starts to the circumstances of the first one and the weather in the second one. Still, I think the Cardinals are going to give New York problems on both sides of the ball, and walk out of MetLife with the win.

The first four games of the modern NFL season is in many ways an extension of training camp. You find out what your team does well and what their issues are that need to be introduced. For the Giants going into their last game of the first quarter of the season, they are actually more unsettled then when the season started due to the losses of their two most important players on the team in consecutive weeks— first Jaxson Dart, then Brian Burns.

What the Giants do best on either side of the ball is it. And with the lackluster performance of Jameis Winston necessitating the trade of J.J. McCarthy , that will be leaned on more for the rest of the season. The face an opponent in the Arizona Cardinals whose rushing defense ranks 26th in the NFL early in the 2026 season, allowing an average of 127.7 rushing yards per game. On offense, they rank 23rd in the NFL but have weapons at running back with Jeremiyah Love, tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Marvin Harrison, Jr.

With rain in the forecast again for gameday, the game will be a replay of last week's win over the Titans. The difference is that Arizona has a proven quarterback in Jacoby Brissett that knows how to win these type of games.

There are two things I can't believe about the Giants after three games. One is that Jameis Winston will continue to put up such woeful numbers. The other is that the Giants' pass rush will continue to be unable to get into the same area code as the opposing quarterback.

Losing Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns in back-to-back weeks is a lot to withstand. There can't be any denying that.

Maybe I am looking at this through blue-colored glasses, but this game could feature big performances by both Winston and the Giants' pass rush. The Giants end up with a feel-good start to their season.

articles.title: Commanders' Jayden Daniels Explains Why He's Not Concerned About Reinjuring Dislocated Elbow
articles.summary: It remains to be seen whether Jayden Daniels will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts just two weeks after he suffered a dislocated left elbow, but the Washington Commanders quarterback isn't worried about reinjuring it.
articles.body:
It remains to be seen whether Jayden Daniels will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts just two weeks after he suffered a dislocated left elbow, but the Washington Commanders quarterback isn't worried about reinjuring it.

"That's what the brace for," he said Thursday, per ESPN's John Keim . "If I had that concern, I would have gotten surgery."

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Daniels has "a chance to play" against the Colts:

It would be a quick turnaround for what appeared to be a significant injury, especially since Daniels also suffered a dislocation in his left arm last season and then reaggravated it five weeks later before he was shut down for the rest of the campaign.

"I'm not surprised," he said when discussing the quick return to the practice field. "Everything I went through, everybody said I would be good to go if I'm able to be out there Sunday. But I'm taking it day by day."

Keim noted the quarterback could still undergo surgery after the season but will be wearing a different brace this time around that keeps his elbow slightly bent in an effort to prevent another dislocation.

"Obviously you have those conversations with people I need to have those conversations with," he said of evaluating his options. "If the surgery was needed to be ASAP, then I've got to do what's best for me. We had those conversations. I was blessed enough to go back out there on the practice field. ... I'm not really concerned at this moment."

Fortunately for the Commanders, they have a solid backup option in place if Daniels cannot play against the Colts.

Marcus Mariota led them to a 33-31 victory over the reigning-champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. He threw three touchdowns and zero interceptions while also adding 11 yards on the ground as a runner.

Daniels gives the team the best chance to win over the long-term course of the season, but many teams would love to have an experienced backup like Mariota to operate the offense in the case of injury.
